handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current supported accent color catalog as the accent_colors KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key accent_colors with the whole supported accent color catalog payload, including listed AccentColor entries and selectable accent color ids in display order.

notes: AccentColor.id is a selector inside the account-level catalog; do not store individual accent colors as independent rows.
Built-in accent color ids 0-6 are always supported and are omitted from updateAccentColors.colors by TDLib.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current global active emoji reaction list as the active_emoji_reactions KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key active_emoji_reactions with the whole emojis vector payload, preserving the TDLib order as the current global list of active emoji reactions.

notes: The update carries one account/global catalog field, not a chat-owned ChatAvailableReactions value and not a ReactionType payload. Store the root vector<string> directly as KV value.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist every active gift auction state from the snapshot and publish the current active-auctions list.

steps.description: For every element in states, persist the GiftAuctionState storage path: persist the nested Gift and Gift.auction_info dependencies, then upsert telegram_gift_auction_states keyed by GiftAuctionState.gift.auction_info.id with gift_id and the full AuctionState payload.

Publish the complete current active gift auction state list from the update so live UI consumers can replace their active-auctions view without treating absence from the list as deletion of unrelated cached auction-state rows.

notes: No separate table or KV entry exists for the active-auctions list; durable storage is the GiftAuctionState facet, while the list snapshot is a live update event.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the active live-location message snapshots, then replace the current active live-location message set.

steps.description: Persist every message in the messages vector through the canonical Message storage path keyed by chat_id and id.

Replace the current active live-location message set with chat_id and message_id for every message in the complete messages vector. An empty vector clears the set; canonical message payloads remain in telegram_messages.

notes: The active set is stored separately from telegram_messages because it is current application state, not a Message field or message history.

handlerPlan.summary: Hydrate the active notification snapshot: persist nested message rows, replace active notification groups and flattened active notifications, record file references, and publish the snapshot change.

steps.condition: a notification in groups has type notificationTypeNewMessage with a message payload
steps.description: Persist every nested notificationTypeNewMessage.message through the canonical Message storage path before storing notification rows that reference that message.

Replace the active notification group table from the snapshot groups. Store group id, NotificationGroupType discriminator, chat id, and total count; notifications are flattened into telegram_active_notifications instead of embedded as a JSONB vector.

Replace flattened active notifications from all groups. Store the active notification identity and type discriminator; for notificationTypeNewMessage store a reference to telegram_messages plus show_preview, for notificationTypeNewCall store call_id, and for notificationTypeNewPushMessage store the push-only payload fields because TDLib says the message may be absent from chat history.
Discover and record file references inside active notification payloads, including notificationTypeNewMessage.message content and notificationTypeNewPushMessage.content media.
Publish that the active notification snapshot has been hydrated so consumers can refresh active notification state from storage.

notes: Run the storage steps in one transaction because updateActiveNotifications is a snapshot sent before incremental updateNotification and updateNotificationGroup updates.

No related KV entry is used for this update; NotificationGroup and Notification are active-state rows, while NotificationGroupType and NotificationType are normalized into discriminators and type-specific columns.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist or clear the current account-level age verification parameters KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key age_verification_parameters with the whole ageVerificationParameters constructor payload.
Delete key age_verification_parameters when TDLib reports that age verification is no longer needed.

notes: AgeVerificationParameters has no durable row identity; min_age, verification_bot_username, and country are stored only as fields inside the opaque telegram_kv.value payload.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the clicked animated-emoji Sticker payload, then publish a live playback request for the addressed message without mutating Message state.

steps.description: Persist the animated sticker through the established Sticker storage path, including its canonical sticker file reference.
Publish a live playback request containing chat_id, message_id, and sticker so UI can play the big animated sticker only when the addressed message is visible; Message row state is not changed.

notes: chat_id and message_id address an existing Message for UI playback and chat action decisions; they do not mutate telegram_messages.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current animation search provider and suggested emoji list as the animation_search_parameters KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key animation_search_parameters with the provider string and the whole emojis vector payload, preserving TDLib order as the current animation search parameters snapshot.

notes: The update carries account-level animation search configuration with no TDLib entity id or owner row; store the root provider and emoji vector together as one KV value.
provider is not an OptionValue; getOption("animation_search_bot_username") identifies the bot flow, while this update supplies the current search provider name and suggested emojis.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the reCAPTCHA verification challenge as a live event so the application can complete or abort it with setApplicationVerificationToken; do not persist the challenge.

steps.description: Publish a live reCAPTCHA verification request containing verification_id, action, and recaptcha_key_id. Consumers must use these values to perform reCAPTCHA and then call setApplicationVerificationToken with the verification_id and resulting token, or an empty token to abort.

notes: This update has no storage review table, KV entry, or delegated TDLib type target. The challenge is request-scoped live state; all root fields are used only for the event payload and are intentionally not stored.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the live application-verification challenge without storing its nonce or verification parameters.

steps.description: Publish verification_id, nonce, and cloud_project_number so the application-verification flow can complete Play Integrity or iOS verification and later call setApplicationVerificationToken with the resulting token or an empty token to abort. Do not persist this one-time challenge in the database.

notes: tdlibStorageReview.json has no table or KV storage target for updateApplicationVerificationRequired; the update is a live verification challenge rather than durable Telegram state.
nonce is one-time verification material and must remain event/effect payload only.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the current attachment and side menu bot facet set from the TDLib snapshot.

steps.description: Replace telegram_attachment_menu_bots with the complete bots vector keyed by bot_user_id. Persist nested File references through their canonical file ids and remove stale facet rows absent from the snapshot.
Publish that the current attachment and side menu bot list changed after the replacement write.

notes: updateAttachmentMenuBots.bots is a complete replacement list; stale rows must be removed in the same storage operation.
AttachmentMenuBot is a facet keyed by bot_user_id = User.id; do not merge it into telegram_users and do not conflate AttachmentMenuBot.is_added with User.added_to_attachment_menu.
Removing a bot facet must not delete canonical telegram_files rows referenced by its icon fields.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current TDLib authorization state as the authorization_state KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key authorization_state with the whole authorization_state constructor payload.

notes: This is the target handler plan; the existing console-only implementation must be replaced when handlers are generated from the plan.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace or reset one scoped autosave settings pair addressed by AutosaveSettingsScope.

steps.description: Delete the row keyed by the canonical AutosaveSettingsScope scope_key when TDLib reports that the scope is reset to default.
Derive scope_key from the AutosaveSettingsScope constructor, then upsert the paired ScopeAutosaveSettings value fields for that scope.
Publish the scoped autosave settings change after storage, including the canonical scope key and whether the scope now has explicit settings or was reset.

notes: Null settings means reset or remove the scoped pair; do not persist a null ScopeAutosaveSettings payload.
The canonical scope key is private_chats, group_chats, channel_chats, or chat:<chat_id> for autosaveSettingsScopeChat.
AutosaveSettingsScope and ScopeAutosaveSettings are stored only as the pair table telegram_autosave_settings.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current available message effect id catalog as one KV snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert key available_message_effects with the complete replacement snapshot containing reaction_effect_ids and sticker_effect_ids in TDLib order. The ids are MessageEffect.id selectors, not reaction rows, sticker file ids, or hydrated MessageEffect payloads.

notes: The update carries only MessageEffect id vectors; individual MessageEffect payloads are returned by getMessageEffect(effect_id) and are not present in this update.
No MessageEffect storage review entry exists in the current state, so this plan stores availability ids only.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the canonical BasicGroup row when TDLib reports changed basic group data.

steps.description: Persist the whole basic_group payload through the BasicGroup storage path keyed by basic_group.id, updating only BasicGroup-owned columns and preserving BasicGroupFullInfo extension columns.

notes: BasicGroupFullInfo extension columns on telegram_basic_groups are not part of updateBasicGroup and must not be overwritten by this handler.
telegram_basic_groups non-key columns are nullable because the row is assembled from BasicGroup and BasicGroupFullInfo updates.

handlerPlan.summary: Merge BasicGroupFullInfo into BasicGroup extension columns keyed by external basic_group_id.

steps.description: Persist File payloads reachable through basic_group_full_info.photo before ChatPhoto and BasicGroup extension storage. This keeps durable File rows explicit instead of hiding them inside owner JSONB.
Persist the nested ChatPhoto payload through the ChatPhoto storage path before the BasicGroup extension row stores photo_id.

Merge the BasicGroupFullInfo extension into telegram_basic_groups using basic_group_id as telegram_basic_groups.id; write only full-info extension columns from basic_group_full_info, store photo as photo_id referencing telegram_chat_photos.id, and preserve BasicGroup-owned columns.

notes: BasicGroupFullInfo has no own id; the storage owner key is external Update.updateBasicGroupFullInfo.basic_group_id.
The plan covers both root fields because the extension payload cannot be keyed without basic_group_id.
members and invite_link remain as current BasicGroup extension JSONB under the existing schema; splitting them into canonical member/invite-link tables is a separate schema-design decision.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the durable BusinessConnection row from the incoming connection payload.

steps.description: Upsert the BusinessConnection row keyed by connection.id. Store id, user_id, user_chat_id, date as timestamptz, nullable rights as embedded BusinessBotRights JSONB, and is_enabled. Disabled connections keep the row with is_enabled=false and rights cleared.
Publish the updated business connection snapshot after the row write for live consumers that track bot business connection state.

notes: BusinessConnection is keyed by its own string id, not by user_id or user_chat_id.
BusinessBotRights has no independent row identity and may be null when the connection is disabled.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the edited business-message snapshot under its business connection, record nested file references, and publish the message update.

steps.description: Persist BusinessMessage.message through the canonical Message storage path keyed by nested chat_id and id, using update semantics because the edited payload replaces current message state.
Persist BusinessMessage.reply_to_message through the canonical Message storage path before storing the nullable reply reference.

Upsert the business-message row keyed by update.connection_id plus BusinessMessage.message.chat_id and BusinessMessage.message.id; store nullable reply_to_message chat/id from the same BusinessMessage payload.
Discover and record file references in BusinessMessage.message and, when present, BusinessMessage.reply_to_message after the corresponding Message rows are stored.
Publish the existing message-updated event from BusinessMessage.message after storage; the business row keeps connection-specific ownership while message views refresh through chat_id/message_id.

notes: BusinessMessage does not carry connection_id; the telegram_business_messages upsert step consumes both update.connection_id and update.message.
Store nested Message rows before telegram_business_messages because message and reply_to_message references target telegram_messages.
This update carries a full BusinessMessage snapshot, not an updateMessageContent-style content delta.

handlerPlan.summary: Delete business-message rows for the affected business connection, chat, and message ids.

steps.description: Delete stored BusinessMessage rows where connection_id equals update.connection_id, message_chat_id equals update.chat_id, and message_id is one of update.message_ids. Do not match by message_id alone and do not delete rows for other business connections or chats.
Publish a deletion event carrying the business connection id, chat id, deleted message ids, and deletion timestamp so live consumers can remove business-message entries.

notes: The update has no from_cache or is_permanent fields, so the handler treats it as authoritative for the BusinessMessage cache.
Do not delete telegram_messages here. BusinessMessage deletion is scoped to the business-message ownership row; generic Message lifetime needs a separate ownership/ref-count decision.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the active one-to-one Call row and publish a sanitized call-state refresh event.

steps.description: Upsert the active Call row keyed by Call.id, storing unique_id, user_id, is_outgoing, is_video, and the embedded CallState payload in telegram_calls.state.
Publish a sanitized call refresh event after storage using call id, user id, direction/video flags, unique_id, and state constructor; do not publish raw transport secrets from callStateReady.

notes: CallState, CallProtocol, CallServer, CallServerType, CallDiscardReason, and Error remain embedded under telegram_calls.state through the Call storage path.
Call.id is the active-call primary key even though it is not persistent history identity; Call.unique_id is stored as linkage only and can be 0 before assignment.
Raw CallState can contain encryption and transport details; the event payload must be sanitized even though the cache row stores the TDLib state snapshot.

handlerPlan.summary: Apply the chat accent/profile color update as a partial Chat row upsert, then publish a chat directory refresh.

steps.description: Upsert the chat row fragment keyed by chat_id, replacing the chat accent color id, reply/link-preview background custom emoji id, embedded upgraded gift colors payload, profile accent color id, and profile background custom emoji id carried by the update.
Publish a chat directory refresh for the affected chat after the row fragment is stored.

notes: This is a partial Chat update; implementation must update only the named telegram_chats columns and must not clear unrelated Chat row state from the sparse update.
upgraded_gift_colors is stored as embedded JSONB on telegram_chats.upgraded_gift_colors; do not create an independent UpgradedGiftColors storage path.
accent_color_id and profile_accent_color_id select existing account-level color catalogs; this update does not mutate those catalogs.
Preserve TDLib sentinel values as current state: background_custom_emoji_id 0 means none, profile_accent_color_id -1 means none, and profile_background_custom_emoji_id 0 means none.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the live chat action event scoped by chat, optional topic, sender, and ChatAction constructor; do not persist active actions.

steps.description: Publish the event target declared by the received ChatAction constructor: chat_action_typing, chat_action_recording_video, chat_action_uploading_video, chat_action_recording_voice_note, chat_action_uploading_voice_note, chat_action_uploading_photo, chat_action_uploading_document, chat_action_choosing_sticker, chat_action_choosing_location, chat_action_choosing_contact, chat_action_start_playing_game, chat_action_recording_video_note, chat_action_uploading_video_note, chat_action_watching_animations, or chat_action_cancel. Include chat_id, nullable topic_id, sender_id, the action constructor, and constructor payload fields such as progress or emoji in the live event payload.

notes: ChatAction is storage=event; chat_id, topic_id, and sender_id scope delivery only and must not create or update durable active-action rows.
chatActionCancel is a live cancel event, not a durable row deletion.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the nullable Chat.action_bar value for one chat and publish a chat refresh.

steps.description: Upsert the chat row fragment keyed by chat_id, replacing telegram_chats.action_bar with the ChatActionBar payload or null when TDLib clears the action bar.
Publish a chat directory refresh for the affected chat after the action_bar field is stored or cleared.

notes: This is a partial Chat update; update only telegram_chats.action_bar and do not clear unrelated Chat row columns.
ChatActionBar and nested AccountInfo remain embedded JSONB inside telegram_chats.action_bar; no independent action-bar table or delegated canonical row is created.

steps.description: Persist the received Background through the canonical Background storage path before recording it as the selected default background.

Upsert key default_background:dark when for_dark_theme is true, otherwise default_background:light. Store a compact selection payload containing the selected Background.id; do not duplicate the Background row payload.
Delete the scoped default-background key for the reported theme when TDLib clears the default background.
Replace default-background file slots for the light/dark scope from the received background; clear that scope slots when background is null.
Publish the account default-background change after storage and file-slot consequences are applied, carrying for_dark_theme and the selected background id or null.

notes: No dedicated default-background table exists in the current metadata; use telegram_kv for the account-level light/dark selection.

Do not derive or rewrite telegram_backgrounds.is_default for older rows from this update. Store only the received Background payload and the current scoped selection.
Null background clears the scoped selection; telegram_kv.value is non-null, so deletion is the clean storage shape.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current account-level default paid reaction selector as the default_paid_reaction_type KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key default_paid_reaction_type with the whole PaidReactionType constructor payload from type. Store paidReactionTypeRegular, paidReactionTypeAnonymous, or paidReactionTypeChat with chat_id inside the JSONB value.

The update field is non-null in TDLib schema, so no delete/reset branch is needed.
No publishEvent or runEffect is needed.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current account default reaction type as the default_reaction_type KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key default_reaction_type with the whole reaction_type constructor payload from the update.

notes: ReactionType is a discriminated value, not a standalone table row. Store the full reactionTypeEmoji, reactionTypeCustomEmoji, or reactionTypePaid payload as the account-level default_reaction_type value.
Do not canonicalize this as a MessageReaction key and do not create standalone ReactionType storage.
No publishEvent or runEffect step is needed.

steps.description: Publish the deletion event with chat id, message ids, permanence, cache flag, and deletion timestamp.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current supported dice emoji catalog as the dice_emojis KV payload.

notes: The update carries one account/global catalog field, not an Emojis wrapper and not StickerSet.emojis.
Store the root vector<string> directly as a complete replacement KV value.
No publishEvent or runEffect is needed.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist a complete direct-messages topic snapshot, including its nested last message reference, then publish the topic refresh.

steps.description: Persist the nested last_message payload through the canonical Message storage path before storing topic last-message reference columns.
Upsert the complete direct messages chat topic row keyed by topic.chat_id and topic.id, including scalar state, embedded sender_id and draft_message, and nullable last_message reference columns.
Discover and record file references inside the nested last_message payload after the message and topic rows are stored.
Publish topic update with chat_id and topic id so subscribers can refresh direct-messages topic state from durable storage.

notes: This update is a complete durable DirectMessagesChatTopic snapshot, not an event-only signal.
No delete or replaceRows semantics are implied by this update.
The draft_message column currently stores embedded JSONB; handler implementation must preserve clear/null semantics for absent draft messages.
Draft-message file ownership is not modeled yet; this plan records files from topic.last_message only.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist nested canonical backgrounds, replace the emoji chat theme catalog KV snapshot, record reachable files, and publish the catalog refresh.

steps.condition: any chat_themes light_settings.background or dark_settings.background is not null
steps.description: Persist every non-null Background payload nested in EmojiChatTheme light and dark ThemeSettings through the canonical Background storage path before replacing the emoji chat theme catalog.

Upsert static key emoji_chat_themes with the complete replacement list of EmojiChatTheme payloads in TDLib order. Preserve theme names and light/dark ThemeSettings; nested Background values are also persisted canonically by the prior step.

steps.condition: chat_themes contains background document or thumbnail file references
steps.description: Replace file slots owned by the emoji_chat_themes catalog from file references reachable through light/dark ThemeSettings.background after Background storage is updated.
Publish that the account emoji chat theme catalog has been replaced after durable storage and file-slot consequences are applied.

notes: EmojiChatTheme.name is a selector inside the catalog, not an independent row key.
updateEmojiChatThemes.chat_themes is a full replacement list; do not merge per-theme rows or leave stale per-theme catalog state.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current ordered favorite sticker file-id list as the favorite_stickers KV snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert static key favorite_stickers with the complete sticker_ids vector, preserving TDLib order as the current list of favorite sticker File.id values. An empty vector clears the list. Do not upsert telegram_stickers because the update carries identifiers only, not Sticker payloads.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the canonical File row, then apply file-subsystem consequences.

steps.description: Upsert the canonical file row from the TDLib File payload.
Apply file-subsystem consequences after the canonical file row is stored: assets, queue, completed-file handling, and owner notifications.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the added FileDownload facet and the current download-list counts, then publish a download-list refresh.

steps.description: Persist file_download.message through the canonical Message storage path before writing the FileDownload facet reference.
Persist the FileDownload facet keyed by file_download.file_id, including add_date, complete_date, is_paused, and the stored message reference.
Upsert key downloaded_file_counts with the whole DownloadedFileCounts payload from counts.
Publish a download-list refresh after the new FileDownload facet and aggregate counts are stored.

notes: Do not create or upsert a canonical File row from this update; file_download carries only file_id, and File state is hydrated by File-returning procedures or updateFile.
Do not route file_download into the app file subsystem as a runEffect unless durable file-subsystem table writes are modeled explicitly first.
The FileDownload complete_date field uses TDLib 0 for not-completed state; handler implementation must preserve that clear state when mapping to timestamp storage.

handlerPlan.summary: Patch the existing FileDownload facet for one file and replace the current downloaded-file counts aggregate.

steps.description: Patch the existing FileDownload facet row keyed by file_id with the new completion timestamp and pause state. Preserve message_chat_id, message_id, and add_date from the existing facet row because updateFileDownload does not carry them.
Upsert key downloaded_file_counts with the whole DownloadedFileCounts payload from counts as the latest account-level download-list aggregate.
Publish that one download-list facet and the aggregate counts changed after durable storage is updated.

notes: Do not use delegateType because updateFileDownload does not carry a FileDownload constructor payload.
Do not route this through files.handleUpdateFile; updateFileDownload carries no File.local or File.remote state.
This is a patch of a hydrated download-list facet. It must not clear FileDownload.message or FileDownload.add_date.
The table currently requires add_date and message reference columns, so a handler must treat a missing facet row as a hydration gap instead of inserting an incomplete row.
TDLib complete_date is 0 when the download is not completed; handler implementation must map that state deliberately instead of treating epoch as a real completion time.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current TDLib file download-list byte and item totals as one KV snapshot and publish the aggregate change.

steps.description: Upsert static key file_downloads_state with total_size, total_count, and downloaded_size as one account-level snapshot. Do not merge this payload with downloaded_file_counts, which stores active/paused/completed counts.
Publish the updated download-list totals after storage so live consumers can refresh from the stored account-level snapshot.

No file-subsystem runEffect is needed because this update does not carry File, FileDownload, file_id, message, or local file state.

handlerPlan.summary: Store the generated-file work request, then start the file-generation side effect.

steps.description: Upsert the current TDLib file-generation request keyed by generation_id with source path, destination path, and conversion token.

Cancel or finalize any in-process application-side generation work for the generation_id. Do not delete canonical File rows.

notes: This update ends the generation request lifecycle; it is not a canonical file deletion.

handlerPlan.summary: Remove the file-download facet row, refresh downloaded-file counts, then publish the download-list change.

steps.description: Delete only the FileDownload facet row for file_id. Keep the canonical telegram_files row and any message rows intact.
Upsert the static downloaded_file_counts KV entry with the new DownloadedFileCounts payload.
Publish that the file was removed from the TDLib download list.

handlerPlan.summary: Upsert mutable forum-topic state for a chat/topic identity and publish the topic-state change.

Publish that the current bot can manage bot_user_id, carrying creator user_id and bot_user_id after the relationship row is written.

handlerPlan.summary: Update the addressed message unread-poll-votes flag, update the chat unread poll vote count, and publish message and chat refresh events.

Upsert the chat row fragment keyed by chat_id, replacing only telegram_chats.unread_poll_vote_count with the new int32 count. Store 0 as a real value, not as absence.
Publish a message refresh for the affected chat_id/message_id after telegram_messages.contains_unread_poll_votes is stored.
Publish a chat directory refresh for the affected chat after telegram_chats.unread_poll_vote_count is stored.

This is a partial Message and partial Chat update; update only the listed columns and do not clear unrelated nullable columns.
No file effect, cache invalidation effect, or TDLib type delegation is required.

handlerPlan.summary: Update message content for an existing message, record any file references, and publish message update.

steps.description: Upsert the message row fragment keyed by chat_id and message_id with the new content payload and transformed edit date when available.
Discover and record file references inside the new content payload.
Publish message update DTO derived from chat id, message id, new content, text/entities/service action helpers, and transformed edit date when available.

notes: edit_date is handled by the TypeScript parser but is not present in the current TDLib docs schema JSON.

handlerPlan.summary: Apply content-opened state to an existing stored Message content payload and publish a message update; do not create a key-only message row.

steps.description: Return without writes when the addressed Message content is not stored locally; this update carries no Message or MessageContent payload and must not create a partial message row.

steps.description: Patch the existing content JSONB in place: for messageVoiceNote set is_listened to true; for messageVideoNote set is_viewed to true. Preserve every other content field and leave all other message columns unchanged. The prior guard makes this update-only despite the generic upsertTable operation.
Publish a message update for the addressed message using the post-update stored content so subscribers refresh listened/viewed state.

notes: updateMessageContentOpened contains only chat_id and message_id; it is not a MessageContent replacement.
TDLib also starts the self-destruct timer, but the update carries no remaining duration or deadline. Do not write telegram_messages.self_destruct_in from this update.
For constructors other than messageVoiceNote and messageVideoNote, durable content JSON remains unchanged; the publish step still reports that the addressed message content was opened.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace a message edit date and reply markup without touching message content, then publish a message refresh.

steps.description: Upsert the message row fragment keyed by chat_id and message_id, replacing only edit_date and reply_markup. A null reply_markup clears telegram_messages.reply_markup. Do not modify telegram_messages.content because TDLib sends content edits separately through updateMessageContent.
Publish a message update after storage using a refreshed stored message/read model; do not emit a content-shaped update that clears content-owned fields for an edit-date/reply-markup-only update.

notes: updateMessageEdited.reply_markup is an embedded ReplyMarkup owner-field replacement on Message.
Changes in message content are delivered separately by updateMessageContent.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the fact-check payload on a message row and publish the message state change.

steps.description: Upsert the message row fragment keyed by chat_id and message_id, replacing telegram_messages.fact_check with the complete update.fact_check payload. Do not merge nested FactCheck text/entities with the previous value.
Publish a message update for chat_id and message_id after durable storage changes, carrying or refreshing the fresh fact_check value.

notes: FactCheck is embedded message state stored in telegram_messages.fact_check; no delegateType step is needed.
The update replaces the whole fact_check value for the addressed Message, not individual FactCheck.text or country_code fields.
No file-system effect is required because FactCheck contains formatted text and country_code only.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace stored interaction_info without nested reactions, replace the message-row reaction state from the nested reactions payload, and publish a message update.

Publish that the addressed message changed after storage. Build the event from refreshed stored message state, not from the sparse update payload alone.

handlerPlan.summary: Update the addressed message pinned flag and publish a message refresh.

Publish a message refresh for the affected chat_id/message_id after telegram_messages.is_pinned is stored. Build the event from refreshed stored message state, not from this sparse update payload alone.

notes: This is a partial Message update; update only the listed columns and do not clear unrelated nullable columns.
This update is not chat-list pinning and must not touch telegram_chat_positions.is_pinned.
No file effect, cache invalidation effect, or TDLib type delegation is required.

handlerPlan.summary: Acknowledge a viewed live-location message signal without mutating durable message or active live-location state.

steps.description: Use chat_id and message_id only to acknowledge that TDLib reported a viewed live-location message. The read-only cache does not request refreshes and the update carries no Message payload, MessageContent payload, viewed timestamp, actor, or location value to store.

notes: Do not store viewed state from this update; TDLib provides no viewed timestamp, actor, location payload, or message content replacement.
If TDLib later sends a Message or updateMessageContent payload, that payload is persisted by the canonical message storage path.

handlerPlan.summary: Mark one message mention as read, replace the chat unread mention count, and publish message and chat refresh events.

steps.description: Upsert the message row fragment keyed by chat_id and message_id, setting telegram_messages.contains_unread_mention to false from the update constructor semantics. Do not mutate message content, unread poll votes, unread reactions, or other Message columns.
Upsert the chat row fragment keyed by chat_id, replacing only telegram_chats.unread_mention_count with the new int32 count. Store 0 as a real value, not as absence.
Publish a message refresh for the affected chat_id/message_id after telegram_messages.contains_unread_mention is stored.
Publish a chat directory refresh for the affected chat after telegram_chats.unread_mention_count is stored.

notes: This update carries no Message payload; do not delegate Message or replace a full message row.
contains_unread_mention is set to false from the update constructor semantics: TDLib says the addressed unread mention was read.
No file effect, cache invalidation effect, or TDLib type delegation is required.

handlerPlan.summary: Apply the public actor reaction delta to telegram_messages.reactions and publish a message refresh.

steps.condition: old_reaction_types and new_reaction_types contain the same canonical ReactionType set
steps.description: Return without DB writes or event publication when the actor reaction set did not change after canonicalizing ReactionType values.

Within a transaction, lock the addressed message row by chat_id and message_id, read telegram_messages.reactions, apply removed and added ReactionType deltas to the embedded reaction summary list, and write the updated JSONB value back to telegram_messages.reactions. Removed reactions decrement total_count and disappear when the count reaches 0; added reactions increment or create a summary item; current-account actor updates is_chosen and used_sender_id.

Publish a message refresh for the affected chat_id/message_id after the embedded reaction-state delta is stored. Use date as occurredAt for the reaction change and build message display data from refreshed stored state.

notes: ReactionType values must be canonicalized before set comparison or embedded summary lookup.
This update is a delta, not a full replacement. Do not replace the whole Message row or interaction_info.
No root update field is ignored. No runEffect is required.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the stored message-row reaction summary list for one message and publish a message update event using the TDLib reaction-change timestamp.

steps.description: For the addressed message row, replace the reaction summary list in telegram_messages.reactions with the update reactions vector. Do not replace telegram_messages.interaction_info because this update carries reaction summaries but not view_count, forward_count, reply_info, or full MessageReactions metadata.
Publish that the addressed message reaction state changed after durable storage. Use date as occurredAt for the reaction change and build display data from refreshed stored state.

notes: Do not use delegateType because updateMessageReactions supplies owner keys plus a vector of child payloads, not a standalone Message payload.
Do not patch telegram_messages.interaction_info from this update.

handlerPlan.summary: Mark an existing temporary outgoing message as acknowledged by the Telegram server and publish a message refresh.

steps.condition: no telegram_messages row exists for chat_id and message_id
steps.description: Return without writes or events when the temporary message is not stored locally; this update carries no Message payload and must not create a key-only partial message row.

For the existing message row keyed by chat_id and temporary message_id, set telegram_messages.send_acknowledged to true. Preserve sending_state and every other message column; updateMessageSendSucceeded or updateMessageSendFailed will later replace the send lifecycle state from a full Message payload.
Publish a message refresh for the addressed temporary message after the acknowledged flag is stored.

notes: TDLib says this update may be sent multiple times for the same message; setting the stored flag to true is idempotent.
The update has no timestamp, success/failure result, or MessageSendingState payload. Do not infer successful delivery or clear sending_state from this update.
The generic upsertTable op is constrained by the preceding guard to update an existing message row only.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the failed Message snapshot, remove stale rows for the previous temporary message id when TDLib remaps it, record file references, and publish an explicit send-failure event.

steps.description: Persist the failed message through the Message storage path with update-on-conflict semantics. This replaces the stored temporary outgoing message state, stores interaction_info without nested reactions, and stores reaction state on telegram_messages.reactions.
Delete file-slot ownership rows for the previous temporary message id after the failed Message snapshot has been persisted under message.id.
Delete the old temporary message row keyed by message.chat_id and old_message_id. Do not delete when old_message_id equals message.id.
Discover and record file references inside the failed Message payload after stale old-message file slots have been removed.

Publish a send-failure event carrying chat id from message.chat_id, failed message id from message.id, old_message_id, and the root Error payload. Build message display data from refreshed stored Message state; use the root error as the explicit failure cause for consumers.

notes: The root error is not a standalone table record. Error remains embedded; durable failed-send state lives in telegram_messages.sending_state through the Message payload.
Do not clear telegram_messages.send_acknowledged. That flag means the quick-ack update was observed, not that sending succeeded.
Do not update Chat.last_message_id here. Chat last-message state is owned by updateChatLastMessage/updateNewChat paths.
Do not record live coverage for a failed outgoing message.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the temporary outgoing message with the final sent Message payload, clean stale temporary-message storage, record files under the final id, and publish a send-success replacement event.

The Message storage path stores interaction_info without nested reactions and stores the final reaction state on telegram_messages.reactions.

For the final message row, clear telegram_messages.send_acknowledged because server acknowledgment is temporary send-attempt state and the successful final Message is now represented by message.id, message.sending_state, and the full Message payload.
Discover and record file references inside the final sent Message payload under the final message owner id.
Delete file slot rows owned by the previous temporary message id after final-message file slots have been recorded.
Delete the stale temporary message row keyed by message.chat_id and old_message_id after the final message row has been persisted.
Publish a replacement event carrying both the previous temporary message reference and the final message reference/DTO so consumers can replace the local optimistic message with the sent message id.

notes: old_message_id is a selector for stale temporary-message cleanup; it is not stored as a column on the final message row.
The final Message payload is authoritative: any field can differ from the optimistic temporary message, including scheduling_state and sending_state.
Do not publish only telegram.message.updated: consumers need old_message_id to replace the temporary local item.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the suggested-post info payload on the addressed message row and publish a message refresh.

Publish a chat directory refresh for the affected chat after telegram_chats.unread_reaction_count is stored.

Discover and record file references in BusinessMessage.message and, when present, BusinessMessage.reply_to_message after the corresponding Message rows are stored.

Discover and record file references in BusinessMessage.message and, when present, BusinessMessage.reply_to_message after the corresponding Message rows are stored.

notes: BusinessMessage does not carry connection_id; update.connection_id supplies the first key segment for telegram_business_messages.
The nested Message rows must be persisted before telegram_business_messages because the business table has hard foreign keys to telegram_messages.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the live chosen inline result event for bot consumers; do not persist chosen-result, user-location, user, or inline-message state.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the opaque bot-only custom event through the Telegram custom extension boundary; do not persist or interpret the JSON string as Telegram domain state.
