handlerPlan.summary: Publish the bot paid-media purchase notification as a live event; do not persist purchase, user, paid-media, payment, or Star transaction state.

steps.description: Publish a live bot paid-media purchase event carrying the buyer User.id scalar reference and the bot-specified paid-media payload. Do not persist the notification, materialize User state, store payload as Invoice, PaymentForm, PaymentReceipt, PaidMedia, or StarTransaction state, fetch transaction history, refund, or log the raw payload.

notes: TDLib marks this update as bot-only and exposes only user_id:int53 plus payload:string.
user_id is a scalar User.id reference; the update does not carry a User payload.
payload is opaque bot correlation data for the paid media purchase, not an Invoice object and not a PaidMedia payload.
PaidMedia storage review explicitly says updatePaidMediaPurchased carries no PaidMedia object and creates no separate PaidMedia storage owner.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the transient bot pending-text message scoped by chat, forum topic, and draft id; do not persist it as Message, DraftMessage, or standalone FormattedText storage.

steps.description: Publish the transient pending text message for Dashboard rendering. Include chat_id, forum_topic_id where 0 means no forum topic, draft_id, text.text, and text.entities; consumers replace any visible pending message with the same draft_id in the same message thread.

notes: updatePendingTextMessage carries no Message payload and no message_id, so it must not write telegram_messages.
draft_id is the generated-text pending draft identifier within the message thread, not DraftMessage storage.
FormattedText and TextEntity remain embedded payload values; updatePendingTextMessage.text must not create standalone text/entity rows.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the canonical Poll snapshot and its poll-option child rows from the bot-only updatePoll payload.

steps.description: Upsert the canonical poll row keyed by poll.id from the complete update poll payload. Store scalar fields and embedded JSONB values, including question, options snapshot, recent_voter_ids, type, and vote_restriction_reason; do not treat message chat_id/message_id as the Poll owner.

Replace all option rows for poll.id with one row per poll.options element keyed by 0-based option_position. An empty options vector clears rows for that poll. Store PollOption.id as payload data because TDLib says it may be empty before assignment.
Publish that the canonical poll snapshot changed so consumers can refresh poll state by poll.id. Do not publish telegram.message.updated because updatePoll has no chat_id or message_id.

notes: updatePoll carries a complete Poll snapshot; do not merge individual option rows incrementally or leave stale options absent from the vector.
PollType is embedded in telegram_polls.type; do not create PollType rows.
Store JSON null for nullable TDLib payloads in not-null JSONB columns such as media, author, and vote_restriction_reason.
telegram_polls.options and telegram_poll_options duplicate option state by design and must be written from the same update.poll in one transaction.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the current selected poll-answer option rows for one poll voter and publish the bot-facing answer change.

steps.description: Replace all current answer-option rows for poll_id plus normalized voter_id with rows derived by zipping option_ids and option_positions by vector index. Empty vectors clear all stored answer-option rows for this voter. Store both the string option id and the 0-based option position; do not mutate Poll, PollOption aggregates, voter counts, recent voters, or is_chosen fields from this update.

Publish the poll answer change for bot consumers after durable current-answer storage is replaced. Carry poll_id, voter_id, option_ids, and option_positions. Do not publish telegram.message.updated because this update has no chat_id or message_id.

notes: MessageSender remains an embedded typed reference encoded as a normalized voter_id key; do not delegate to a standalone MessageSender table.
The update carries no Poll or PollOption payload, so do not delegate Poll, replace Poll rows, or replace PollOption rows.
No runEffect is required. Durable answer state is explicit DB storage, not hidden behind an effect.
The handler must treat option_ids and option_positions as parallel vectors with equal length.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current supported profile accent color catalog as the profile_accent_colors KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert key profile_accent_colors with the whole supported profile accent color catalog payload, including listed ProfileAccentColor entries and selectable profile accent color ids in display order.

notes: ProfileAccentColor.id is a selector inside the account-level profile_accent_colors catalog; do not store individual profile accent colors as independent rows.
ProfileAccentColors stays embedded inside each ProfileAccentColor light_theme_colors and dark_theme_colors payload.
No publishEvent or runEffect is required for this storage-only catalog update.

handlerPlan.summary: Upsert the quick-reply shortcut row, persist its nested first quick-reply message with the parent shortcut id, record file references, and publish the shortcut update.

steps.description: Upsert shortcut.first_message as a QuickReplyMessage row before the shortcut row is written. Use shortcut.first_message.id as the message primary key, inject shortcut.id into telegram_quick_reply_messages.shortcut_id, and store order 0 because this payload is the first shortcut message. Store nullable embedded sending_state and reply_markup as JSONB null values when TDLib sends null.
Upsert the durable quick-reply shortcut row keyed by shortcut.id. Store name, message_count, and first_message_id from shortcut.first_message.id after the nested first message row exists.
After durable storage, record file references reachable through shortcut.first_message.content and shortcut.first_message.reply_markup.
Publish that the quick-reply shortcut basic state changed after the shortcut and nested first-message rows are stored.

notes: Do not replace the full quick-reply message list from this update. updateQuickReplyShortcut carries only basic shortcut data and the first message snapshot.
Write telegram_quick_reply_messages before telegram_quick_reply_shortcuts because telegram_quick_reply_shortcuts.first_message_id has a hard FK to telegram_quick_reply_messages.id.
telegram_quick_reply_messages.shortcut_id is intentionally not an FK because the shortcut table already points back to first_message_id.

handlerPlan.summary: Delete the quick-reply shortcut row and all stored quick-reply message rows owned by the deleted shortcut id, then publish deletion.

steps.description: Delete the shortcut row keyed by shortcut_id before deleting message rows, because telegram_quick_reply_shortcuts.first_message_id references telegram_quick_reply_messages.id.
Delete all quick-reply message rows whose owner shortcut_id matches the deleted shortcut id.
Publish that the shortcut and its quick-reply message list were deleted.

notes: Do not delegate QuickReplyShortcut because the update carries only shortcut_id.
Do not delete canonical Message rows; these are QuickReplyMessage rows in telegram_quick_reply_messages.
If quick-reply file-owner rows are added later, add an explicit runEffect for file-owner cleanup.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the stored quick-reply message list for one shortcut, record file references, and publish the shortcut-message list change.

steps.description: Replace all quick-reply message rows for shortcut_id with the complete messages vector from this update. Set shortcut_id on every row from the update root field, store the 0-based vector index as order, and map each quickReplyMessage payload into telegram_quick_reply_messages. An empty messages vector clears all rows for this shortcut.
After row replacement, discover file references inside quickReplyMessage.content, quickReplyMessage.reply_markup, and nested embedded payloads.
Publish that the stored quick-reply message list changed for the shortcut.

notes: Use replaceRows, not delegateType, because QuickReplyMessage does not carry shortcut_id; the owner key comes from updateQuickReplyShortcutMessages.shortcut_id.
The vector is authoritative for this shortcut. Do not merge it with existing rows or leave stale rows absent from the new vector.
QuickReplyMessage.id is globally unique among quick replies, so telegram_quick_reply_messages.id remains the row primary key while shortcut_id is the owner key for replacement and deletion.
Store sending_state and reply_markup as JSON null in their not-null JSONB columns when TDLib sends null payloads.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current ordered quick-reply shortcut id list as a KV snapshot without mutating canonical shortcut rows.

steps.description: Upsert static key quick_reply_shortcut_ids with the complete shortcut_ids vector, preserving TDLib order as the current account-level quick-reply shortcut order. An empty vector clears the ordered list. Do not upsert or delete telegram_quick_reply_shortcuts rows because this update carries shortcut ids only.

notes: Deletion semantics belong to updateQuickReplyShortcutDeleted, not to ids missing from this ordered list.
Canonical shortcut rows remain owned by updateQuickReplyShortcut.shortcut.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current account-level reaction notification settings as the reaction_notification_settings KV payload.

steps.description: Upsert static key reaction_notification_settings with the whole reactionNotificationSettings payload from notification_settings, replacing message_reaction_source, story_reaction_source, poll_vote_source, sound_id, and show_preview as one account-level settings snapshot.

notes: ReactionNotificationSettings is a singleton account-level current-state value, not an entity table row.
ReactionNotificationSource values remain embedded inside the stored JSONB payload.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current ordered recent sticker file-id list for one recent-sticker bucket as a telegram_kv snapshot keyed by is_attached.

steps.description: Upsert the current sticker_ids vector under a key derived from is_attached: true stores the recently attached sticker list, false stores the recently sent sticker list. Preserve TDLib order. An empty sticker_ids vector clears the current list for that key. Do not upsert telegram_stickers or telegram_files because this update carries File.id identifiers only, not Sticker or File payloads.

notes: is_attached selects exactly one of two recent-sticker lists; the handler must not overwrite the other list.
sticker_ids are File.id values, not Sticker.id values and not Sticker payloads.
No FK should be added from the JSONB vector to telegram_files.id.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current ordered saved animation file-id list as the saved_animations KV snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert static key saved_animations with the complete animation_ids vector, preserving TDLib order as the current list of saved animation File.id values. An empty vector clears the saved-animation list. Do not upsert telegram_files or any Animation row because this update carries identifiers only, not File or Animation payloads.

notes: updateSavedAnimations.animation_ids is vector<int32> of File.id values.
Animation remains embedded in owner payloads; this update does not make Animation a table row.
getSavedAnimations returns hydrated Animation payloads separately, but this update stores only the current saved-id list.
No publishEvent or runEffect is required for this storage-only catalog update.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the saved-message tag rows for one Saved Messages scope from the complete tags payload, then publish the scoped tag-list change.

steps.description: Replace all saved-message tag rows for saved_messages_topic_id with one row per tags.tags item. Use saved_messages_topic_id as the owner scope, where 0 means the whole Saved Messages chat and nonzero values identify one SavedMessagesTopic. Canonicalize each SavedMessagesTag.tag ReactionType into telegram_saved_messages_tags.tag, and store count plus label from the same item. An empty tags vector clears the scoped tag list.
Publish that the saved-message tag list changed for the affected saved_messages_topic_id after the replacement write commits.

notes: SavedMessagesTags is an embedded wrapper around tags; do not create a row for the wrapper itself.
SavedMessagesTag is the durable row shape in telegram_saved_messages_tags, keyed by saved_messages_topic_id plus canonical ReactionType text.
Do not add an FK from saved_messages_topic_id to telegram_saved_messages_topics.id because 0 is a documented all-Saved-Messages sentinel.
ReactionType remains embedded value data and must not get standalone table storage.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist a complete Saved Messages topic snapshot, including its nested last message reference, then publish the topic refresh.

steps.description: Persist the nested last_message payload through the canonical Message storage path before storing telegram_saved_messages_topics.last_message_chat_id and telegram_saved_messages_topics.last_message_id.

Upsert the complete Saved Messages topic row keyed by topic.id. Store topic.type and topic.draft_message as embedded JSONB, store JSON null for draft_message when TDLib sends null, and store nullable last-message reference columns from topic.last_message when present.
Discover and record file references inside the nested last_message payload after durable message and topic storage.
Publish Saved Messages topic update with topic.id so subscribers can refresh topic state from durable storage.

notes: This update is a complete durable SavedMessagesTopic snapshot, not an event-only signal.
No delete or replaceRows semantics are implied by this update.
DraftMessage remains embedded at telegram_saved_messages_topics.draft_message; nested input payload types are not delegated to standalone storage.
Draft-message file ownership is not modeled in current similar plans; this plan records files from topic.last_message only.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current approximate Saved Messages topic count as a KV snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert static key saved_messages_topic_count with topic_count as the current approximate total number of Saved Messages topics. Do not derive this value by counting telegram_saved_messages_topics rows because TDLib marks the value approximate and local topic rows can be incomplete while pagination is not fully loaded.

notes: topic_count is scalar account-level aggregate state, not a SavedMessagesTopic row and not a row replacement command.
No publishEvent or runEffect is needed for the current storage plan; durable storage is explicit in the upsertTable step.
The static key is handler-defined, so telegram_kv.key does not need a dynamic source field for this update.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current ordered saved notification sound id list as a telegram_kv snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert static key saved_notification_sound_ids with the complete notification_sound_ids vector, preserving TDLib order as the current saved notification sound list. An empty vector clears the list. Do not upsert NotificationSound or File rows because this update carries notification sound identifiers only, not NotificationSound or File payloads.

notes: TDLib says this update may not be sent until information about a notification sound was requested for the first time; the KV list is a saved-id catalog snapshot, not proof that every NotificationSound payload is hydrated.

Full NotificationSound payloads are returned by addSavedNotificationSound, getSavedNotificationSound, and getSavedNotificationSounds; those result paths need their own storage decision when procedure result handling is designed.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace one account-level notification settings row addressed by NotificationSettingsScope.

steps.description: Derive scope_key from the NotificationSettingsScope constructor, then upsert the paired ScopeNotificationSettings value fields for that scope. This is a full row replacement for the addressed scope and must not affect the other scope rows.
Publish that account-level scoped notification settings changed after durable storage, carrying the canonical scope key so consumers can refresh the affected scope.

notes: NotificationSettingsScope constructors map to private_chats, group_chats, or channel_chats through telegram_notification_settings.scope_key.keyRule.
ScopeNotificationSettings has no independent identity; it is stored only as the value side of the NotificationSettingsScope pair.
Do not delegate ChatNotificationSettings or mutate per-chat notification settings from this account-scope update.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the canonical SecretChat row when TDLib reports changed secret chat data.

steps.description: Persist the whole secret_chat payload through the SecretChat storage path keyed by secret_chat.id, including the embedded SecretChatState value in telegram_secret_chats.state. Keep key_hash only on the canonical SecretChat row.

notes: SecretChat is a durable table entity keyed by SecretChat.id; updateSecretChat is not event-only.
SecretChatState has no standalone storage and is stored as embedded JSONB in telegram_secret_chats.state.
Do not create or update a Chat row from this update. ChatType.chatTypeSecret references SecretChat.id, but updateSecretChat carries only the SecretChat row.
No publishEvent is added until a concrete consumer event contract is selected.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the incoming service notification as a live popup request without storing it as message or active notification state.

steps.description: Publish a live popup request carrying service notification type and MessageContent payload. If type begins with AUTH_KEY_DROP_, include the Cancel and Log out action contract in the event payload; the destructive Destroy call belongs to the later explicit user action, not to receipt of this update.

notes: Do not write telegram_messages: this update has no chat_id or message_id and MessageContent is not owned by a Message here.
Do not write telegram_active_notifications or telegram_active_notification_groups: TDLib service notifications are popup instructions, not active notification-list state.

Do not delegate nested MessageContent table-shaped payloads from this update. The current storage review treats updateServiceNotification.content as service-popup evidence, not as the durable owner for MessageContent or its nested values.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current non-Premium speech-recognition trial limits as one telegram_kv snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert static key speech_recognition_trial with max_media_duration, weekly_count, left_count, and next_reset_date as one complete current snapshot. Preserve zero values exactly: weekly_count 0 means no free recognitions, and next_reset_date 0 means unknown reset time. Do not update SpeechRecognitionResult or message media state because this update describes account-level trial/quota parameters only.

notes: The four root scalar fields are one coherent quota payload and must be stored together under a static KV key.
SpeechRecognitionResult remains embedded on VideoNote and VoiceNote owner payloads; this update does not carry recognition text, pending state, or errors.
No publishEvent or runEffect is needed for the current storage-only plan.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish a live Premium speed-limit notification for upload or download; do not persist it.

steps.description: Publish a live notification event carrying is_upload and the derived direction: upload when true, download when false. Do not store this in telegram_kv or a table; this update is a prompt/notification signal, not durable file or Premium state. Consumers that need the expected Premium speedup must request the matching TDLib option separately: premium_upload_speedup for upload, premium_download_speedup for download.

notes: The update does not carry File, FileDownload, PremiumLimitType, or an entity id, so there is no delegated type and no DB target.
The notification may be postponed until a visible file exists, but the update itself still carries only the live notification direction.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish the fresh stake dice state as a live event and do not persist the short-lived state hash.

steps.description: Publish the stake_dice_state event carrying the full StakeDiceState payload: state_hash, stake_toncoin_amount, suggested_stake_toncoin_amounts, current_streak, prize_per_mille, and streak_prize_per_mille. Treat state_hash as a short-lived token usable only while recently received; consumers must request getStakeDiceState again after restart or expiry.

notes: StakeDiceState storage is event, not table, embedded, facet, pair, or KV.
Do not persist state_hash in telegram_kv or any table; it is not a durable identity and must not be replayed as cached state.
Empty state_hash and empty prize_per_mille are meaningful live payload values when stake dice cannot be sent by the current user.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the current Telegram Stars revenue status facet for one MessageSender owner.

steps.description: Normalize owner_id from MessageSender into the canonical typed owner key, then upsert the complete StarRevenueStatus snapshot for that owner. Store total_amount, current_amount, and available_amount as StarAmount JSONB payloads preserving star_count and nanostar_count; replace withdrawal_enabled and next_withdrawal_in from the same status payload.

notes: owner_id must include the MessageSender constructor discriminator, so messageSenderUser.user_id and messageSenderChat.chat_id cannot collide.
StarRevenueStatus is current owner-scoped state, not a transaction list and not an account-level balance.
TDLib says an opened transaction screen may call getStarTransactions after this update; this handler must not fetch transactions by itself.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the changed StickerSet snapshot, persist nested File payloads, and record sticker-set file references.

steps.condition: sticker_set carries nested File payloads through thumbnail, stickers, sticker thumbnails, premium animations, or related media payloads
steps.description: Persist every File payload reachable from sticker_set through the canonical File storage path before sticker-set file effects run. Keep Sticker, Thumbnail, StickerFullType, and related payloads embedded in telegram_sticker_sets JSONB columns unless their own table storage path is triggered by a direct owner update.

Persist the whole sticker_set payload through the StickerSet storage path keyed by sticker_set.id. Store scalar fields and embedded JSONB payloads on telegram_sticker_sets, including thumbnail, thumbnail_outline, sticker_type, stickers, and emojis.

Discover and record file references inside the stored sticker_set payload after durable File and StickerSet storage, including set thumbnails, sticker files, sticker thumbnails, and nested premium animation files.

notes: StickerSet is a durable table entity keyed by StickerSet.id; updateStickerSet is not event-only.

StickerSet.stickers is stored as JSONB on telegram_sticker_sets.stickers in the current schema. Do not upsert telegram_stickers from this update unless the table schema is changed to make StickerSet.stickers a direct Sticker row source.
No publishEvent is added until a concrete sticker-set event contract is selected.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the changed Story row, clear stale failed-post metadata, record story file references, and publish the story update.

steps.condition: story.content carries nested File payloads through StoryContent photo/video, PhotoSize.photo, StoryVideo.video, or StoryVideo.thumbnail.file
steps.description: Persist every File payload reachable from story.content through the canonical File storage path before story file-slot effects run. Keep StoryContent, Photo, StoryVideo, Thumbnail, and PhotoSize embedded in telegram_stories.content; only File is delegated to its table.

Persist the complete Story payload through the Story storage path keyed by story.poster_chat_id plus story.id. Convert story.date from Unix timestamp to timestamptz and store nullable embedded payloads according to the Story table contract.
Clear failed-post metadata on the same Story row by setting error and can_post_story_result to SQL null. A normal story update means the retained row is no longer in the failed-post state.
After durable File and Story storage, discover and record file references owned by the Story media payload so the file subsystem can maintain story media slots and download policy state.
Publish that the canonical Story row changed after storage commits, including poster_chat_id and story id so consumers refresh from durable storage.

notes: updateStory is not event-only; Story storage review marks Story as a retained table row keyed by poster_chat_id plus id.
Do not create separate rows for StoryContent, StoryArea, StoryVideo, Photo, Thumbnail, FormattedText, ReactionType, MessageSender, StoryPrivacySettings, StoryRepostInfo, or StoryInteractionInfo.
Do not key Story by id alone; id is unique only among stories posted by the same chat.

handlerPlan.summary: Delete the inaccessible canonical Story row, clean story-owned file slots, and publish the story deletion.

steps.description: Delete only file-slot ownership rows for the story owner key composed from story_poster_chat_id and story_id. Do not delete canonical telegram_files rows; nested File state can be shared by other owners.
Delete the canonical Story row where poster_chat_id equals story_poster_chat_id and id equals story_id. Match the composite key; story_id alone is not globally unique.

Publish that the story became inaccessible after local cleanup, carrying story_poster_chat_id and story_id so consumers can remove the story from views without inferring deletion of the posting chat or nested canonical entities.

notes: Story.id is local to Story.poster_chat_id; never delete by story_id alone.
Do not delete or rewrite ChatActiveStories here. updateChatActiveStories owns the retained active-story summary payload.
Do not delete canonical telegram_files rows when cleaning story media ownership slots.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the active-story chat count for one StoryList selector as a dynamic telegram_kv entry.

steps.description: Upsert dynamic key story_list_chat_count:<StoryList.constructor> derived from story_list with chat_count as the current total number of chats with active stories in that story list. Store 0 as a real value. Do not update telegram_chat_active_stories because this update carries list-level count state only and no per-chat active-story facet payload.

notes: StoryList remains embedded selector data on ChatActiveStories.list and as a selector/key for list-scoped state; this plan stores the count state, not StoryList itself.
The dynamic key must use the StoryList constructor token, not JSON serialization that can drift across runtimes.
chat_count must not be derived from telegram_chat_active_stories rows.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the failed Story snapshot, attach failure metadata to the same story row, record story file references, and publish a story-post-failed event.

steps.condition: story.content carries nested File payloads through StoryContent photo/video, PhotoSize.photo, StoryVideo.video, or StoryVideo.thumbnail.file
steps.description: Persist every File payload reachable from the failed Story through the canonical File storage path before story file-slot effects run.
Persist the failed story through the canonical Story storage path keyed by story.poster_chat_id and story.id. This writes the complete Story payload before failure-only metadata is attached.

Attach failed-post metadata to the same telegram_stories row keyed by story.poster_chat_id and story.id. Store error as embedded Error JSONB. Store error_type as embedded CanPostStoryResult JSONB, or SQL null when TDLib sends null.
Discover and record file references inside the failed Story payload after durable File and Story storage. This is file-subsystem side-effect work, not hidden DB storage for the story row.

Publish that story posting failed after the Story row and failure metadata are stored. Include story key, refreshed story payload/DTO, embedded Error, and nullable CanPostStoryResult failure type for consumers.

notes: Do not store Error or CanPostStoryResult as standalone rows; both are embedded failure metadata on telegram_stories.
Do not treat this as cancellation. TDLib says cancellation is represented by updateStoryDeleted instead.
error_type may be null and must be stored as SQL null in telegram_stories.can_post_story_result.
The failed Story payload remains authoritative for the Story row; the root error fields add failure metadata that Story itself does not natively contain.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the temporary posted story with the final Story payload, clear failure metadata, clean stale temporary-story storage, record files under the final story key, and publish a post-success replacement event.

steps.condition: story.content carries nested File payloads through StoryContent photo/video, PhotoSize.photo, StoryVideo.video, or StoryVideo.thumbnail.file
steps.description: Persist every File payload reachable from the final Story through the canonical File storage path before story file-slot effects run.
Persist the final posted story through the Story storage path keyed by story.poster_chat_id and story.id, replacing any existing final row with the complete Story payload.
Clear failed-post metadata on the final Story row by setting error and can_post_story_result to SQL null. The successful final story replaces failed temporary state.
Discover and record file references reachable from the final Story payload under the final story owner key story.poster_chat_id plus story.id.
Delete file slot rows owned by the previous temporary story key story.poster_chat_id plus old_story_id after final-story file slots have been recorded.

Delete the stale temporary story row keyed by story.poster_chat_id and old_story_id after the final Story row has been persisted. Guard against old_story_id equal to story.id so the final row is never deleted.
Publish a replacement event carrying the previous temporary story reference and the final story reference/DTO so consumers can replace the optimistic story with the posted story id.

notes: old_story_id is a selector for stale temporary-story cleanup; it is not stored as a column on the final Story row.
The final Story payload is authoritative and can differ from the temporary postStory result.
Do not keep both temporary and final story ids as active Story rows.
files.recordStoryFiles and files.deleteStoryFileSlots are target handler work; current Story storage retains nested file references inside embedded Story payload columns.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current account-level story stealth mode timers as one KV snapshot and publish the settings refresh.

steps.description: Upsert static key story_stealth_mode with active_until_date and cooldown_until_date as one complete current snapshot. Preserve 0 values exactly: active_until_date 0 means stealth mode is disabled, and cooldown_until_date 0 means there is no active cooldown.
Publish the refreshed story stealth mode status after the KV snapshot is stored, carrying active_until_date and cooldown_until_date so consumers do not infer state from Story rows.

notes: This update does not carry a Story payload and must not mutate telegram_stories.
The two timestamps are one account-level state snapshot; do not split them into separate KV keys.
No file effect or nested type delegation is needed.

handlerPlan.summary: Apply the suggested-action delta by deleting removed action rows, upserting added action rows, and publishing the changed current-account suggested-action set.

steps.description: For every action in removed_actions, derive the same canonical action_key used for storage and delete that suggested-action row. Use only constructor identity fields for the key: constructor discriminator, suggestedActionCustom.name, and suggestedActionConvertToBroadcastGroup.supergroup_id. Do not use mutable display or payload fields such as title, description, url, authorization_delay, can_be_hidden, or manage_premium_subscription_url for identity.

For every action in added_actions, derive canonical action_key from constructor identity, then upsert one telegram_suggested_actions row. Store constructor-specific payload fields on their columns, store FormattedText title and description as embedded JSONB for suggestedActionCustom, and set nullable payload columns that do not belong to the constructor to SQL null so a reused action_key cannot retain stale variant data.
Publish that the current-account suggested-action set changed after delete and upsert writes commit, carrying enough information for consumers to refresh the suggested-action list from storage.

notes: Process removals before additions so an overlapping action_key ends with the added payload rather than being dropped.
SuggestedAction title and description remain embedded FormattedText JSONB values; do not create TextEntity rows from this update.
No runEffect is required; this update is durable account UI state plus a change notification.
Do not add a hard FK from telegram_suggested_actions.supergroup_id to telegram_supergroups.id; this update carries a scalar id and can arrive before the supergroup row is available.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the canonical Supergroup row when TDLib reports changed supergroup or channel data.

steps.description: Persist the whole supergroup payload through the Supergroup storage path keyed by supergroup.id, updating only Supergroup-owned columns on telegram_supergroups and preserving SupergroupFullInfo extension columns. Convert supergroup.date from Unix timestamp to timestamptz; store Usernames, ChatMemberStatus, VerificationStatus, RestrictionInfo, and ActiveStoryState as embedded JSONB according to the table contract.

notes: updateSupergroup is guaranteed before a supergroup identifier is returned to the application, so this handler must be able to create the base telegram_supergroups row without SupergroupFullInfo data.
Do not create or update telegram_chats from this update. Chat links to Supergroup through Chat.type.chatTypeSupergroup.supergroup_id, but Chat state is owned by Chat updates.
Do not overwrite SupergroupFullInfo extension columns from updateSupergroup; those columns are filled by updateSupergroupFullInfo.
No file effect is required because Supergroup carries no File payload.

handlerPlan.summary: Merge SupergroupFullInfo extension fields into the canonical Supergroup row keyed by external supergroup_id.

steps.condition: supergroup_full_info.photo is not null and carries nested ChatPhoto media files
steps.description: Persist File payloads reachable through supergroup_full_info.photo before ChatPhoto and Supergroup extension storage. This keeps durable File rows explicit instead of hiding them inside media effects.
Persist the nested ChatPhoto payload through the ChatPhoto storage path before the Supergroup extension row stores photo_id.

Merge the SupergroupFullInfo extension into telegram_supergroups using supergroup_id as telegram_supergroups.id. Write only full-info extension columns from supergroup_full_info, store photo as photo_id referencing telegram_chat_photos.id, and preserve Supergroup-owned columns from updateSupergroup. Store nullable owner projections as SQL null when TDLib sends null.
Publish that the Supergroup full-info extension changed after storage commits, carrying supergroup_id so consumers can refresh the Supergroup row from storage.

notes: SupergroupFullInfo has no own id; the storage owner key is external Update.updateSupergroupFullInfo.supergroup_id.
Do not write Supergroup-owned base columns from this update.
Do not treat supergroup_id as chat_id for invite-link storage; telegram_supergroups.invite_link remains an owner projection unless a handler explicitly resolves Chat.id from Supergroup.id.
Do not delete invite-link rows when supergroup_full_info.invite_link is null; TDLib null can mean absent or not visible.
Do not rely on slow_mode_delay_expires_in as self-refreshing state; TDLib says this update is not triggered for every countdown change.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the current pending Telegram terms-of-service row and publish that user action is required.

steps.description: Delete existing pending terms-of-service rows and insert exactly one row keyed by terms_of_service_id. Store terms_of_service.text as embedded FormattedText JSONB, min_user_age as integer, and show_popup as boolean. This keeps the table as current pending account ToS state instead of a historical log.

Publish that a new terms-of-service obligation is pending after durable storage, carrying terms_of_service_id and the stored payload so UI can show the blocking popup when show_popup is true and route acceptance through acceptTermsOfService.

notes: Do not delegate TermsOfService without the update envelope because TermsOfService has no intrinsic id.

acceptTermsOfService, registerUser, and the deleteAccount decline flow must clear this pending table in their own procedure handlers; updateTermsOfService only creates or replaces the pending obligation.
show_popup false is not a reason to skip storage; the terms still need explicit accept or decline handling by id.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the current text-composition style catalog from the authoritative styles vector.

steps.description: Replace telegram_text_composition_styles with one row per TextCompositionStyle in styles, keyed by TextCompositionStyle.name. An empty styles vector clears the catalog. Store english_example as embedded JSONB or SQL null when TDLib sends null. Do not retain rows absent from the replacement vector.

notes: Use replaceTable rather than upsertTable because TDLib sends the new supported-style list and stale names must be removed.
TextCompositionStyleExample remains embedded in telegram_text_composition_styles.english_example; do not create separate example rows.
No publishEvent or runEffect is required for this storage-only catalog update.

handlerPlan.summary: Upsert canonical user row and publish a compact user-updated event.

steps.description: Upsert the canonical user row fragment used by the current handler.
Publish user DTO with id, names, bot/self flags, and username when present.

notes: The current handler stores only the user fields currently consumed by the application, not the full generated User table payload.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current account-level Toncoin revenue status as the ton_revenue_status KV snapshot and publish the revenue-status refresh.

steps.description: Upsert static key ton_revenue_status with the whole TonRevenueStatus payload as the current account-level Toncoin revenue and withdrawal status. Store total_amount, balance_amount, available_amount, and withdrawal_enabled exactly as received; do not convert amounts to display units.

Publish that the current Toncoin revenue status changed after the KV snapshot is stored. Consumers can refresh revenue or transaction views from their own context; this handler does not call TDLib procedures.

notes: TonRevenueStatus is current-user account state, not chat revenue, not owned_ton_count, and not TonTransactions history.
Do not create a separate TonRevenueStatus table: the payload has no standalone primary key or owner key.
TonRevenueStatistics.status must hydrate the same ton_revenue_status snapshot when procedure-result handling is designed.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current topic message count for one Saved Messages or channel direct-messages topic as a dynamic telegram_kv entry.

steps.description: Upsert a dynamic topic message-count key derived from chat_id and topic_id. For messageTopicDirectMessages use topic_message_count:<chat_id>:direct_messages:<direct_messages_chat_topic_id>; for messageTopicSavedMessages use topic_message_count:<chat_id>:saved_messages:<saved_messages_topic_id>. Store message_count as the current TDLib approximate number of messages in that topic, including 0 as a real value. Do not update telegram_direct_messages_chat_topics or telegram_saved_messages_topics because this update carries aggregate count state only and no complete topic row payload.

notes: TDLib documents this update for Saved Messages and channel direct messages chat topics only; the handler must not synthesize storage for messageTopicForum or messageTopicThread from this update.
MessageTopic remains an embedded selector. The stored object here is the count state selected by MessageTopic, not the MessageTopic value itself.
The count must not be derived by counting local Message rows because TDLib marks the value approximate and local history can be incomplete.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current trending sticker-set prefix for one StickerType as a dynamic telegram_kv snapshot.

steps.condition: sticker_sets contains File payloads through StickerSetInfo thumbnails, cover stickers, or nested sticker media
steps.description: Persist every File payload reachable from sticker_sets through the canonical File storage path before storing the trending cache snapshot or running file effects. Keep StickerSetInfo and Sticker summaries embedded in the KV payload; do not upsert canonical StickerSet rows from this list-summary update.

Upsert dynamic key trending_sticker_sets_by_type:<StickerType.constructor> derived from sticker_type with the complete sticker_sets payload as the current cached trending prefix for that sticker type. Preserve total_count, sets order, is_premium, and per-item is_viewed values. Do not update telegram_sticker_sets from StickerSetInfo summaries and do not overwrite caches for other StickerType constructors.
Record file references reachable from the stored trending sticker-set prefix after File rows and the KV snapshot are persisted, including sticker-set thumbnails and cover sticker media.

notes: The key must use the fieldless StickerType constructor token, not JSON serialization of sticker_type and not the is_premium field.
sticker_sets is documented as a prefix; this plan stores the prefix delivered by the update for the supplied sticker_type.
StickerSetInfo.id references canonical StickerSet identity, but this update carries list summary payloads, not full StickerSet rows.
getTrendingStickerSets offset/limit procedure-result caching needs separate merge/window rules and must not corrupt this update prefix snapshot.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist the current account-level trusted Mini App bot user-id list as a static telegram_kv snapshot.

steps.description: Upsert static key trusted_mini_app_bots with the complete bot_user_ids vector, preserving TDLib order as the current list of bot User.id values whose Mini Apps can read clipboard text and open without warning. An empty vector clears the list. Do not delegate User and do not require telegram_users rows, because TDLib states these users may not be delivered by updateUser and may not be accessible.

notes: bot_user_ids are scalar User.id references only, not User payloads.
No FK should be added from the JSONB vector to telegram_users.id.
No publishEvent or runEffect is required for this storage-only account-level trust list.

handlerPlan.summary: Persist or clear the current first unconfirmed session singleton and publish the prompt refresh.

steps.description: Upsert static key unconfirmed_session with the whole unconfirmedSession constructor payload: id, log_in_date, device_model, and location. Keep this as the current first pending session snapshot; do not create a multi-row UnconfirmedSession or Session table record from this update.
Delete static key unconfirmed_session when TDLib reports that there is no current first unconfirmed session.

Publish the prompt state after the KV row is stored or deleted. Carry the current session payload or null so consumers can show the confirmation prompt, dismiss it, and call confirmSession with session.id only after user intent.

notes: The update field is nullable; telegram_kv.value is non-null, so null must delete the static key instead of storing a null JSONB value.
UnconfirmedSession.id shares the active session id namespace and is consumed by confirmSession, but this update maintains only the first pending session singleton.
No runEffect is required. Confirming the session is a later user-driven procedure call, not automatic update handling.

handlerPlan.summary: Store the unread-chat counters for one ChatList selector as a dynamic telegram_kv snapshot and publish a list-count refresh event.

steps.description: Upsert dynamic key unread_chat_count:<ChatList.key> derived from chat_list, storing total_count, unread_count, unread_unmuted_count, marked_as_unread_count, and marked_as_unread_unmuted_count as one JSONB snapshot. Preserve 0 values as real counts. Do not mutate telegram_chats, telegram_chat_positions, or ChatList storage from this aggregate update.
Publish that the unread-chat counters changed for the canonical ChatList key so live consumers can refresh list badges from the stored snapshot.

notes: ChatList remains an embedded selector/key value, not a standalone table row.
total_count is TDLib approximate total for the chat list and must not be recomputed from cached Chat rows.
This update is sent only when the message database is used; absence of the update does not imply zero counters.

handlerPlan.summary: Store unread-message counters for one ChatList selector as a dynamic telegram_kv snapshot and publish a list-count refresh event.

steps.description: Upsert dynamic key unread_message_count:<ChatList.key> derived from chat_list, storing unread_count and unread_unmuted_count as one JSONB snapshot. Preserve 0 values as real counts. Do not mutate telegram_chats, telegram_chat_positions, telegram_messages, or ChatList storage from this aggregate update.
Publish that unread-message counters changed for the canonical ChatList key so live consumers can refresh list badges from the stored snapshot.

notes: ChatList remains an embedded selector/key value, not a standalone table row.
This update stores aggregate counter state for a chat list; it does not update individual Chat.unread_count values or Message read state.
This update is sent only when the message database is used; absence of the update does not imply zero counters.

handlerPlan.summary: Merge the UserFullInfo extension into the canonical User row keyed by external user_id, after persisting nested media rows.

steps.condition: user_full_info contains File payloads through personal_photo, photo, public_photo, first_profile_audio, bot_info media, thumbnails, covers, or nested media values
steps.description: Persist every File payload reachable from user_full_info through the canonical File storage path before storing ChatPhoto rows or the UserFullInfo owner projection. This includes files inside ChatPhoto, Audio, Photo, Animation, Thumbnail, Sticker, and related embedded media values.

steps.condition: user_full_info.personal_photo, user_full_info.photo, or user_full_info.public_photo is not null
steps.description: Persist non-null personal_photo, photo, and public_photo through the ChatPhoto storage path before the User row stores personal_photo_id, photo_id, and public_photo_id references.

Merge the complete UserFullInfo extension into telegram_users using user_id as telegram_users.id. Write only UserFullInfo-owned extension columns from user_full_info and preserve base User columns from updateUser. Store nullable TDLib fields as SQL null when TDLib sends null; store personal_photo, photo, and public_photo as ChatPhoto id references rather than duplicated ChatPhoto JSONB.
Publish that the UserFullInfo extension changed after storage commits, carrying user_id so consumers can refresh the full User row from storage.

notes: UserFullInfo has no native id; the owner key is external Update.updateUserFullInfo.user_id.
Do not delegate User from this update. updateUserFullInfo does not carry the base User payload and must not overwrite base User columns.
Do not use personal_chat_id, ChatPhoto.id, File.id, or Audio.file.id as the UserFullInfo owner key.
Audio remains an embedded owner value in first_profile_audio, with nested File rows persisted through File before the User row projection is written.
BusinessInfo.local_opening_hours, next_open_in, and next_close_in are snapshot fields inside business_info; TDLib says their countdown changes do not trigger updateUserFullInfo.
UserFullInfo personal_photo, photo, and public_photo are stored as references to canonical ChatPhoto rows.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the current account privacy rules for one UserPrivacySetting key.

steps.description: Derive setting_key from the UserPrivacySetting constructor discriminator using telegram_user_privacy_setting_rules.setting_key.keyRule, then replace the stored rules JSONB with the complete UserPrivacySettingRules payload from the update. Preserve rule order exactly; TDLib matches rules in order and the first matched rule defines the result.
Publish that the privacy rules changed for the canonical setting_key after durable storage commits, so live consumers can refresh the affected privacy setting.

notes: This is the same pair addressed by getUserPrivacySettingRules(setting) and setUserPrivacySettingRules(setting, rules).
Do not serialize the whole setting object as a key; use the canonical keyRule constructor mapping.
Do not normalize individual UserPrivacySettingRule items into rows. Rules are ordered embedded values inside UserPrivacySettingRules.rules.
Do not delegate User or Chat from nested rule user_ids/chat_ids. They are selector references inside privacy-rule JSONB, not delivered entity payloads.
No runEffect is required; durable storage is the explicit telegram_user_privacy_setting_rules upsert.

handlerPlan.summary: Replace the embedded status field on the canonical user row by user_id and publish a user-status refresh event.

steps.description: Upsert a telegram_users row fragment keyed by user_id and replace only status with the complete UserStatus constructor payload. Preserve all other telegram_users columns as they are; this update does not carry the full User payload.

Publish that one user online status changed after telegram_users.status is stored. The event must identify the user by user_id and carry or reference the new status payload; it must not require names, usernames, bot flags, or other fields only available from updateUser.

notes: UserStatus remains embedded JSONB on telegram_users.status; do not create a UserStatus table or KV entry.
The handler must not delegate User because updateUserStatus carries only user_id and status, not a User payload.
A status-only row is valid because telegram_users.id is the only non-null column; later updateUser can fill the rest of the canonical row.

handlerPlan.summary: Mark an existing scheduled video message as no longer waiting for video conversion and publish a message refresh.

steps.condition: no telegram_messages row exists for chat_id and message_id
steps.description: Return without writes or events when the addressed message is not stored locally; this update carries no Message payload and must not create a key-only partial message row.

For the existing message row keyed by chat_id and message_id, set telegram_messages.scheduling_state to null. Preserve content, date, edit_date, sending_state, and every other message column because this update only proves that the automatically scheduled video message was sent after conversion; it does not carry a replacement Message payload.
Publish a message refresh for the addressed message after scheduling_state is cleared so consumers stop treating it as waiting for video processing.

notes: This update identifies a converted scheduled video message but carries no Video payload.
Do not delegate Video or File from this update; nested file storage can only come from stored Message/MessageContent payloads or updateFile.
Do not set telegram_messages.date or edit_date from this update because TDLib provides no timestamp here.
The generic upsertTable op is constrained by the preceding guard to update an existing message row only.

handlerPlan.summary: Publish a live close request for the opened Web App launch after TDLib reports that the Web App sent a message; do not persist Web App launch state.

steps.description: Publish that the Web App launch identified by web_app_launch_id must be closed because the opened Web App sent a message. Consumers that own Web App views should close the matching launch and then inform TDLib through closeWebApp(web_app_launch_id) after the view is actually closed. Do not store WebAppInfo, WebApp metadata, message state, or launch state from this update.

notes: web_app_launch_id is a transient launch handle returned by openWebApp, not a durable WebApp id.
This update carries no Message payload; the sent message will arrive through message updates if it is represented in message storage.
Do not create a WebAppInfo table or telegram_kv snapshot for this signal.
Do not use runEffect for durable storage. A future Web App runtime may subscribe to telegram.web_app.close_requested; the handler plan only defines the Telegram update consequence.
KV storage writes the whole current constructor payload into telegram_kv.value; fields are not mapped to physical columns.

reviews.decision: AccentColor is one item in the account-level supported accent color catalog delivered by updateAccentColors; owner payloads store only accent_color_id selectors.

directUpdateUse: updateChatAccentColors.accent_color_id:int32 applies a selected AccentColor.id to Chat state
indirectTypeUse: Payloads containing Chat, User, ChatInviteLinkInfo, PageBlock.chatLink, SponsoredMessage, or ChatEventAction carry AccentColor only as scalar id references
procedureUse: setAccentColor.accent_color_id:int32 selects an AccentColor.id for the current user
setChatAccentColor.accent_color_id:int32 selects an AccentColor.id for a chat

rejectedStorage.table: AccentColor.id is a catalog selector inside the account-level snapshot; updateAccentColors replaces the supported-color list and no procedure or update mutates one AccentColor row by id.
rejectedStorage.embedded: The AccentColor payload is not stored inside Chat, User, or message payload fields; those owners store scalar accent_color_id references while the catalog is rooted at accent_colors.
rejectedStorage.extend: AccentColor is not a one-to-one structural extension of a single owner row.
rejectedStorage.facet: There is no Chat, User, or other domain owner key for one AccentColor facet record; the state is an account/global catalog.
rejectedStorage.pair: AccentColor is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.event: Supported accent colors are current catalog state needed after update delivery and restart, not live-only signals.

notes: AccentColor.id looks table-like, but updateAccentColors replaces the account-level catalog; do not model individual colors as independently updated rows.
updateAccentColors.colors omits built-in ids 0-6, so absence from that list does not mean the accent color id is unsupported.
Agrees with maturity 1 because the existing entry's kv/accent_colors decision is supported; no detailed maturity 1 review is present to critique beyond confirming that target.

reviews.decision: AcceptedGiftTypes is a flag value stored only as GiftSettings.accepted_gift_types; procedures mutate the containing GiftSettings, not this value independently.

procedureUse: setBusinessAccountGiftSettings(business_connection_id, settings.accepted_gift_types) mutates a business account gift-settings value

rejectedStorage.table: AcceptedGiftTypes has no stable id or row key; its boolean fields are payload inside GiftSettings.
rejectedStorage.extend: It does not structurally extend one externally identified owner row; it is one field of GiftSettings.
rejectedStorage.facet: No procedure or update addresses AcceptedGiftTypes as a separate owner-keyed aspect; owner keys apply to the containing GiftSettings value.
rejectedStorage.pair: There is no key/value companion type; the five flags form one value object.
rejectedStorage.kv: The value belongs to GiftSettings/UserFullInfo or a GiftSettings procedure input, not an unowned account/global singleton.
rejectedStorage.event: Accepted gift settings are durable current state, not a live-only signal.

notes: Agrees with maturity 1 because the existing storage entry stores AcceptedGiftTypes as embedded at GiftSettings.accepted_gift_types; no separate maturity 1 storage-decision review exists, and maturity 2 evidence confirms that target.

reviews.decision: AccountInfo has no own identity and appears only as the nullable account_info field on the ChatActionBar report/add/block variant.

procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns AccountInfo or ChatActionBar directly.
Chat-returning procedures can contain Chat.action_bar -> ChatActionBar.account_info.
chatActionBarReportAddBlock action procedures identify chat/user state externally and do not address AccountInfo as stored state.

rejectedStorage.table: AccountInfo has no stable id or local key; any owner identity comes from the surrounding Chat.action_bar state.
rejectedStorage.extend: It does not structurally extend Chat, User, or another owner row; it is one optional field on a ChatActionBar variant.
rejectedStorage.facet: updateChatActionBar replaces the action_bar value scoped by chat_id; AccountInfo is not a separate owner-scoped aspect record.
rejectedStorage.pair: There is no companion key/value type; the object is a standalone nested payload.
rejectedStorage.kv: The value is tied to a specific ChatActionBar in a chat, not an account-level or global stable name.
rejectedStorage.event: This is current action-bar state delivered through Chat and updateChatActionBar, not a live-only signal.

notes: Agrees with maturity 1 because the existing decision stores AccountInfo as embedded at ChatActionBar.account_info, and maturity 2 evidence confirms it has no independent identity, no direct update use, and no direct procedure use.

reviews.decision: ActiveStoryState is only a nullable state value on the canonical Supergroup and User rows; it has no owner key or independent lifecycle outside those owner fields.

rejectedStorage.table: activeStoryStateLive.story_id is a nested live story identifier, not an ActiveStoryState row identity, and the type has no owner id or separately addressed lifecycle.
rejectedStorage.extend: The value does not structurally extend exactly one owner type; it is a nullable field used by both Supergroup and User.
rejectedStorage.facet: There is no separate owner-scoped ActiveStoryState update or procedure shape; updateUser and updateSupergroup replace it as part of the owner row.
rejectedStorage.pair: The type is not stored as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.kv: The value belongs to specific Supergroup or User owner rows, not to an account-level singleton key.
rejectedStorage.event: The value represents current owner state that must remain with the retained owner row, not a live-only signal.

notes: activeStoryStateLive.story_id identifies the live story within the owner context; do not treat it as the storage key for ActiveStoryState.

Agrees with maturity 1 because the existing embedded decision remains correct: maturity 2 evidence shows ActiveStoryState appears only as Supergroup.active_story_state and User.active_story_state, with no direct update or procedure identity. No separate maturity 1 storage-decision review block for ActiveStoryState was present to critique.

reviews.decision: Address is a plain value with no own identity. Durable storage keeps it as nested payment/order and passport element fields; direct shipping-query and input-passport occurrences are operation payloads, not Address storage.

indirectTypeUse: MessageContent.order_info, PaymentFormType.saved_order_info, and PaymentReceiptType.order_info expose Address through OrderInfo.shipping_address
PassportElements.elements and PassportElementsWithErrors.elements expose Address through PassportElement.address
indirectUpdateUse: message update paths can carry Address through MessageContent.order_info
procedureUse: getSavedOrderInfo returns OrderInfo.shipping_address; validateOrderInfo accepts OrderInfo.shipping_address and can save owner order info when allow_save is true; deleteSavedOrderInfo removes the saved owner value
getPaymentForm and getPaymentReceipt can return Address through payment form or receipt OrderInfo fields

setPassportElement accepts InputPassportElement.address and returns PassportElement.address; getPassportElement, getAllPassportElements, and getPassportAuthorizationFormAvailableElements return PassportElement.address; deletePassportElement removes the owning passport element
answerShippingQuery responds to the updateNewShippingQuery id but does not make shipping_address stored Address state

rejectedStorage.table: Address has no id or stable local key; query ids, passport element type, and order/payment contexts identify owners or operations, not Address rows.
rejectedStorage.extend: Address is reused by multiple owner payloads and does not structurally extend exactly one owner row.
rejectedStorage.facet: No procedure or update addresses a separate owner-keyed Address record; procedures address order info, passport elements, or shipping queries.
rejectedStorage.pair: Address is not stored only as a key/value association with a companion type.
rejectedStorage.kv: Address values belong to concrete order/passport/query payloads, not account-level or global singleton state.
rejectedStorage.event: updateNewShippingQuery carries an event payload, but Address also appears in durable order and passport payloads, so the type is not live-only.

notes: PassportElement.address is security-sensitive passport data and PassportElement has no existing storage entry; keep Address embedded in the owning passport element instead of duplicating it in a generic address cache.
updateNewShippingQuery.shipping_address is scoped by the shipping query id for response handling only; do not use the update envelope as an Address storage target.

Changes maturity 1 from no recorded Address storage-decision review and the existing OrderInfo.shipping_address-only target to OrderInfo.shipping_address, PassportElement.address because PassportElement.address is a durable owner field returned and mutated by passport element procedures, while InputPassportElement.address and updateNewShippingQuery.shipping_address remain input/update evidence only.

reviews.decision: AffiliateProgramInfo has no own identifier and represents the current affiliate program field of a bot. Persistent storage belongs to BotInfo.affiliate_program; FoundAffiliateProgram.info is a fresh search result payload and does not define a second persistent owner.

rejectedStorage.table: AffiliateProgramInfo has no stable local or global identifier; bot_user_id appears on FoundAffiliateProgram and procedure inputs, not on this type as row identity.
rejectedStorage.extend: This value does not structurally extend one owner row as full-info data; it is a nullable field inside BotInfo.
rejectedStorage.facet: The state can be stored as the BotInfo.affiliate_program field without losing the write shape; the chat_id used by setChatAffiliateProgram identifies the affected bot, not a separate AffiliateProgramInfo record.
rejectedStorage.pair: The type is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.kv: The value is bot-owned state, not an account-level or global singleton keyed by a stable domain name.
rejectedStorage.event: The active affiliate program is current bot state returned through UserFullInfo/BotInfo and must survive beyond live event delivery.

notes: FoundAffiliateProgram.info is returned by searchAffiliatePrograms with bot_user_id on the wrapper; do not create a persistent AffiliateProgramInfo row from this fresh search payload.
setChatAffiliateProgram mutates this embedded bot field by chat_id and parameters, so implementation must resolve the affected bot owner before replacing BotInfo.affiliate_program.
Agrees with maturity 1 classification: AffiliateProgramInfo remains embedded at BotInfo.affiliate_program; maturity 2 adds explicit update, procedure, and fresh search-result evidence.

reviews.decision: AffiliateProgramParameters has no own identity; it is a two-field value owned by affiliate-program payloads. Store it embedded where TDLib exposes durable/current affiliate-program state: AffiliateProgramInfo.parameters for active bot programs and ConnectedAffiliateProgram.parameters for connected affiliate-program records. setChatAffiliateProgram uses the same shape as an input replacement for BotInfo.affiliate_program, not as standalone parameters storage.

indirectUpdateUse: updateUserFullInfo.user_full_info via UserFullInfo.bot_info via BotInfo.affiliate_program via AffiliateProgramInfo.parameters
procedureUse: getUserFullInfo -> UserFullInfo.bot_info via BotInfo.affiliate_program via AffiliateProgramInfo.parameters
searchAffiliatePrograms -> FoundAffiliatePrograms.programs via FoundAffiliateProgram.info via AffiliateProgramInfo.parameters

rejectedStorage.table: AffiliateProgramParameters has no id or stable local key; commission_per_mille and month_count are scalar values, while chat_id, bot_user_id, affiliate, and url appear on owners or procedures, not on this type as row identity.
rejectedStorage.extend: The type does not structurally extend exactly one owner row; it is a nested parameter value reused by affiliate-program payloads.
rejectedStorage.facet: External owner keys on setChatAffiliateProgram and connected-affiliate procedures address the owning affiliate-program state, not a separate owner-scoped parameters record.
rejectedStorage.pair: The type is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.kv: The value belongs to affiliate-program owners, not to an account-level or global singleton keyed by a stable domain name.
rejectedStorage.event: The parameters describe current affiliate-program state returned by procedures and UserFullInfo paths; they are not live-only event payloads.

notes: setChatAffiliateProgram.parameters is an input replacement scoped by chat_id and may be null to close the active program; do not persist the function argument as a standalone parameters row.
ConnectedAffiliateProgram has no existing storage review; keep AffiliateProgramParameters embedded in that owner value and classify the connected-program owner key separately.

Changes maturity 1 from AffiliateProgramInfo.parameters to AffiliateProgramInfo.parameters, ConnectedAffiliateProgram.parameters because ConnectedAffiliateProgram.parameters is a second direct owner returned by connected-affiliate procedures, while setChatAffiliateProgram.parameters remains input-only and FoundAffiliateProgram.info remains an AffiliateProgramInfo path rather than a separate parameters owner.
KV storage writes the whole current constructor payload into telegram_kv.value; fields are not mapped to physical columns.

reviews.decision: AgeVerificationParameters is a current-account singleton snapshot delivered by updateAgeVerificationParameters.parameters, nullable when verification is not needed, with no entity id or owner field. Store the latest account-level value under the stable kv key age_verification_parameters.

indirectUpdateUse: RestrictionInfo.has_sensitive_content description references updateAgeVerificationParameters as the source of age-verification gating for sensitive content
procedureUse: getOption("can_ignore_sensitive_content_restrictions") is referenced by RestrictionInfo.has_sensitive_content for checking whether restrictions can be ignored
setOption("ignore_sensitive_content_restrictions", OptionValue) is referenced by RestrictionInfo.has_sensitive_content after the user passes age verification

rejectedStorage.table: The constructor has no durable row identity; min_age, verification_bot_username, and country are payload values, not stable primary keys for AgeVerificationParameters rows.
rejectedStorage.embedded: The value is delivered by a root account-level update, not as a field of Chat, User, RestrictionInfo, or another owner payload; embedding it under an owner would lose the update and null-clear shape.
rejectedStorage.extend: It does not structurally extend a single owner row identified outside the object; the only owner context is the current account.
rejectedStorage.facet: There is no Chat/User/Message or other domain owner key; this is one current-account value, not an owner-scoped aspect record.
rejectedStorage.pair: No separate key-shape/value-shape association exists; the persistent key is the domain kv name.
rejectedStorage.event: The update represents current account state needed after live delivery, and null clears that state; it is not a live-only signal.

notes: updateAgeVerificationParameters.parameters may be null, so the kv entry must be cleared or stored as null when age verification is no longer needed.
verification_bot_username and country are payload fields used for the verification flow and localization; do not key storage by bot username or country.

reviews.decision: AlternativeVideo is an embedded media-quality value on messageVideo.alternative_videos. reviews.decision: BusinessOpeningHours has no durable identity of its own.
