Store it embedded in both BusinessInfo fields; BusinessOpeningHoursInterval remains embedded under BusinessOpeningHours.opening_hours.

procedureUse: setBusinessOpeningHours(opening_hours:businessOpeningHours|null) accepts the type directly and mutates the current user BusinessInfo.opening_hours field
getUserFullInfo(user_id:int53) returns UserFullInfo, which can include BusinessInfo.opening_hours and BusinessInfo.local_opening_hours

rejectedStorage.table: BusinessOpeningHours has no id or stable local key. time_zone_id identifies a time zone, not a row, and setBusinessOpeningHours replaces/removes the current user BusinessInfo.opening_hours value instead of addressing an opening-hours row.
rejectedStorage.extend: BusinessOpeningHours is not a full-info extension of User, BusinessInfo, or another owner row; it is a nested field value and can appear in two fields on BusinessInfo.
rejectedStorage.facet: The user/current-user scope belongs to the containing UserFullInfo.business_info owner. BusinessOpeningHours has no separate one-per-owner update or result shape that would justify a facet outside the BusinessInfo field.
rejectedStorage.pair: BusinessOpeningHours is not stored only as an association between a key type and a value type.
rejectedStorage.kv: BusinessOpeningHours is not an account-level or global singleton; it belongs to concrete BusinessInfo fields for a UserFullInfo owner.
rejectedStorage.event: BusinessOpeningHours represents current business profile state returned by getUserFullInfo and changed by setBusinessOpeningHours, so it must be retained with owner state rather than emitted only as a live signal.

notes: BusinessInfo.local_opening_hours uses the same TDLib type but is derived local-time state whose field changes do not trigger updateUserFullInfo; setter writes must update or invalidate BusinessInfo.opening_hours and refresh local_opening_hours through getUserFullInfo before treating it as fresh.

Agrees with the existing maturity 2 embedded target. The reviewed owner BusinessInfo is embedded at UserFullInfo.business_info, UserFullInfo is reviewed as extend User, and BusinessOpeningHoursInterval is already targeted as embedded under BusinessOpeningHours.opening_hours; no reviewed target supports a table, facet, or kv split.

reviews.decision: BusinessOpeningHoursInterval has no own identity or independent lifecycle. It is one bounded minute range inside BusinessOpeningHours.opening_hours; getUserFullInfo and updateUserFullInfo carry it only through UserFullInfo.business_info.opening_hours or local_opening_hours, and setBusinessOpeningHours replaces the containing BusinessOpeningHours value for the current user. Store the interval embedded in BusinessOpeningHours.opening_hours.

procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns BusinessOpeningHoursInterval directly.
setBusinessOpeningHours(opening_hours:businessOpeningHours|null) mutates the current user BusinessInfo.opening_hours value, whose opening_hours field contains BusinessOpeningHoursInterval items

rejectedStorage.table: BusinessOpeningHoursInterval has no id, stable local key, or procedure/update shape that addresses one interval row independently; start_minute and end_minute are value bounds, not a durable row identity.
rejectedStorage.extend: The interval is not a one-to-one structural extension of an externally identified owner row; many intervals can exist inside one BusinessOpeningHours value.
rejectedStorage.facet: No owner key addresses BusinessOpeningHoursInterval as a separate aspect. UserFullInfo and setBusinessOpeningHours replace the containing BusinessOpeningHours value instead of addressing interval state separately.
rejectedStorage.pair: BusinessOpeningHoursInterval is not stored only as an association between a key type and a value type; its two integer fields form one embedded range value.
rejectedStorage.kv: The interval belongs to BusinessOpeningHours under BusinessInfo, not to an account/global singleton keyed by a stable domain name.
rejectedStorage.event: Opening-hours intervals are current business profile state returned by getUserFullInfo and set through setBusinessOpeningHours, not live-only signals.

notes: Changes the prior stub-level entry by preserving embedded storage at BusinessOpeningHours.opening_hours while adding the missing constructor, use, procedure, rejection, and owner-chain evidence. BusinessOpeningHours is reviewed as embedded at BusinessInfo.opening_hours and BusinessInfo.local_opening_hours; BusinessInfo is reviewed as embedded at UserFullInfo.business_info; UserFullInfo is reviewed as extend User.

reviews.decision: BusinessRecipients is a selector value stored in owner recipient fields, not an independently addressable row. Its chat_ids and excluded_chat_ids are Chat.id reference lists inside the value, and the remaining fields are boolean selection flags. updateUserFullInfo and current-account setters replace the containing away/greeting settings or connected-bot settings; removeBusinessConnectedBotFromChat mutates BusinessConnectedBot.recipients.excluded_chat_ids, but the owner is still the connected-bot settings value rather than BusinessRecipients itself.

procedureUse: setBusinessAwayMessageSettings(away_message_settings.recipients) mutates the current user's BusinessInfo.away_message_settings value
setBusinessGreetingMessageSettings(greeting_message_settings.recipients) mutates the current user's BusinessInfo.greeting_message_settings value
setBusinessConnectedBot(bot.recipients) adds or changes the current-account connected bot settings
deleteBusinessConnectedBot(bot_user_id) removes the containing current-account connected bot settings

rejectedStorage.table: BusinessRecipients has no durable id or stable local key of its own. chat_ids and excluded_chat_ids are referenced Chat.id lists inside the owner field, and no procedure addresses a BusinessRecipients row.
rejectedStorage.extend: BusinessRecipients does not structurally extend exactly one owner row; it is reused by away message settings, greeting message settings, and connected bot settings.
rejectedStorage.facet: The current-account connected-bot procedures and updateUserFullInfo owner paths identify containing settings values, not a separately stored one-per-owner BusinessRecipients aspect.
rejectedStorage.pair: The type is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape; the recipient selection fields form one embedded value.
rejectedStorage.kv: BusinessRecipients is not an unowned account/global singleton. Each occurrence belongs to a specific owner field.
rejectedStorage.event: Recipient selections are durable configuration used by later settings reads and mutations, not live-only signals.

notes: chat_ids and excluded_chat_ids are Chat.id reference lists inside the embedded value; do not treat them as BusinessRecipients row keys or duplicate Chat payload.
removeBusinessConnectedBotFromChat applies only to BusinessConnectedBot.recipients.excluded_chat_ids for the current connected bot; do not apply that mutation shape to away or greeting recipients.

Changes the previous embedded target by adding BusinessConnectedBot.recipients, which is a direct schema owner used by getBusinessConnectedBot, setBusinessConnectedBot, and removeBusinessConnectedBotFromChat. The embedded storage kind remains correct because the type has no identity outside its owner fields.

reviews.decision: BusinessStartPage has no identity or owner key. It is the nullable BusinessInfo.start_page value carried by UserFullInfo.business_info; updateUserFullInfo and getUserFullInfo replace or return it through UserFullInfo, and setBusinessStartPage mutates the same current-user field using InputBusinessStartPage rather than addressing a BusinessStartPage record. Store it embedded at BusinessInfo.start_page, with sticker stored as a reference to Sticker.id.

procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns BusinessStartPage directly.
setBusinessStartPage(start_page:inputBusinessStartPage|null) mutates the current user BusinessInfo.start_page output field

rejectedStorage.table: BusinessStartPage has no id or stable local key, and no update or procedure addresses one start-page row independently of the containing BusinessInfo/UserFullInfo owner.
rejectedStorage.extend: BusinessStartPage is not a full-info extension of an externally identified owner row; it is one nullable field inside BusinessInfo.
rejectedStorage.facet: The external user_id from updateUserFullInfo/getUserFullInfo and the implicit current-user setter scope identify the containing UserFullInfo.business_info state, not a separate one-per-user BusinessStartPage facet; the schema exposes it as an ordinary BusinessInfo field.
rejectedStorage.pair: BusinessStartPage is not stored only as an association between separate key and value TDLib types.
rejectedStorage.kv: BusinessStartPage is not an account/global singleton keyed by a stable domain name. It belongs to a specific UserFullInfo.business_info value.
rejectedStorage.event: BusinessStartPage is current business profile state returned by getUserFullInfo, replaced by updateUserFullInfo, and changed by setBusinessStartPage, so it must be retained with owner state rather than emitted live-only.

notes: BusinessStartPage.sticker is a Sticker table value keyed by Sticker.id; store a Sticker reference inside the embedded start-page value instead of duplicating the sticker entity payload.

Confirms the previous maturity 2 embedded classification after checking the owner chain BusinessInfo -> UserFullInfo, the current-user setter shape, and referenced storage targets BusinessInfo, UserFullInfo, and Sticker. BusinessInfo is embedded at UserFullInfo.business_info, UserFullInfo extends User, and Sticker is a table keyed by id.

reviews.decision: ButtonStyle is a field-only button style enum stored as the style value on InlineKeyboardButton and KeyboardButton. It has no fields, no independent identity, and all durable appearances flow through the owning button values inside ReplyMarkup rows.

indirectTypeUse: Message.reply_markup, QuickReplyMessage.reply_markup, and InputInlineQueryResult.reply_markup expose ButtonStyle through ReplyMarkup rows
indirectUpdateUse: message, business-message, and quick-reply update paths can carry ButtonStyle through owner reply_markup fields
procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns ButtonStyle directly.
sendMessage, sendBusinessMessage, editMessage*, editBusinessMessage*, editInlineMessage*, stopPoll, and stopBusinessPoll accept ReplyMarkup values that can contain ButtonStyle through rows
getPreparedKeyboardButton returns KeyboardButton.style for prepared request buttons
message-returning and business-message-returning procedures can return ButtonStyle through Message.reply_markup or BusinessMessage reply markup owners

rejectedStorage.table: ButtonStyle has no id, local key, fields, or independently addressed row lifecycle; it is only a nested enum-like value.
rejectedStorage.extend: ButtonStyle does not structurally extend one owner row; it is a field on two button value types.
rejectedStorage.facet: No update or procedure addresses ButtonStyle as a separate owner-keyed aspect; owner keys apply to messages or reply markup containing the button.
rejectedStorage.pair: ButtonStyle is not stored as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.kv: ButtonStyle is not an account-level or global cached value; each occurrence belongs to a concrete button field.
rejectedStorage.event: ButtonStyle can be part of durable reply markup state on messages, quick replies, and inline results, so it is not a live-only signal.

notes: Confirms the existing maturity 2 storage entry: embedded at InlineKeyboardButton.style and KeyboardButton.style. Referenced owner decisions for InlineKeyboardButton and KeyboardButton are also embedded in ReplyMarkup.rows, so storing ButtonStyle as a nested button field matches the accepted owner chain.

reviews.decision: Call is active one-to-one call state keyed by Call.id. updateCall creates or replaces the row, createCall returns the same active-call id, and active call procedures, notifications, and signaling updates address the row by call_id. Call.unique_id is persistent call-history linkage, not the active row key.

directTypeUse: CallId.id:int32 returns active Call.id from createCall
MessageContent.messageCall.unique_id:int64 stores ended-call history identity corresponding to Call.unique_id when non-zero
directUpdateUse: updateCall.call:call creates or replaces the active Call row
indirectTypeUse: Message.content embeds messageCall.unique_id:int64 for ended-call history
Call.user_id:int53 references the existing User table keyed by id
Call.state:CallState uses the existing embedded target Call.state
indirectUpdateUse: Message-bearing updates can carry Message.content.messageCall.unique_id for ended-call history, separate from the active Call row
procedureUse: createCall(user_id, protocol, is_video) returns CallId.id; updateCall supplies the Call row
acceptCall(call_id, protocol) mutates an incoming Call by Call.id
discardCall(call_id, is_disconnected, invite_link, duration, is_video, connection_id) ends a Call by Call.id
sendCallSignalingData(call_id, data) sends active-call signaling data by Call.id

sendCallDebugInformation(call_id:InputCall), sendCallLog(call_id:InputCall), and sendCallRating(call_id:InputCall) use either inputCallDiscarded.call_id or inputCallFromMessage(chat_id,message_id) for ended-call reporting
searchCallMessages returns FoundMessages containing call-message history; deleteAllCallMessages deletes call-message history, not active Call rows

rejectedStorage.embedded: Call is delivered as a root update and addressed by call_id in active-call procedures, notifications, and signaling; embedding it under User, Notification, or Message would lose the active call row lifecycle.
rejectedStorage.extend: Call has user_id, but it is not a one-to-one structural extension of User; it is an active interaction with its own id and state.
rejectedStorage.facet: Call.id is the active call identity itself, not an external owner key for a user-scoped aspect.
rejectedStorage.pair: Call is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.kv: Call state is keyed by active call id and is not an account-level or global singleton snapshot.
rejectedStorage.event: updateCall carries current state needed by accept, discard, signaling, rating, log, and debug procedures; updateNewCallSignalingData is live payload but does not make Call itself live-only.

notes: Call.id is explicitly not persistent; store active Call rows as session-scoped cache and do not use it as ended-call history identity.

Call.unique_id is persistent but can be 0 before server assignment and is used by MessageContent.messageCall/InputCallFromMessage linkage, so it must not replace Call.id as the active-call primary key.
Call.state can include callStateReady.encryption_key and call transport details; avoid duplicating that sensitive live state outside the active Call row.

Keeps the existing table decision and fills its missing target with id. The target is Call.id because updateCall, createCall, active notifications, signaling updates, and active-call procedures use call_id; related accepted targets inspected were User.id, CallState at Call.state, NotificationType at Notification.type, and MessageContent at Message.content.

reviews.decision: CallbackQueryPayload is live callback-query payload carried by incoming callback-query updates and by getCallbackQueryAnswer as an action input. It has no identity and no durable owner; persisting it would cache transient bot interaction data instead of retained Telegram state.

rejectedStorage.table: CallbackQueryPayload has no id or stable local key; query id, chat_id, message_id, inline_message_id, connection_id, and chat_instance are fields on callback-query update/procedure envelopes, not row identity on the payload type.
rejectedStorage.embedded: The only owner fields are live callback-query update payloads and the getCallbackQueryAnswer input; no durable Chat, Message, BusinessMessage, or inline-message owner stores this payload as retained state.
rejectedStorage.extend: It is not a one-to-one structural extension of a Chat, Message, BusinessConnection, User, or other owner row.
rejectedStorage.facet: External owner keys on callback-query updates identify the live query context, but the payload itself is not a separately retained owner-scoped aspect.
rejectedStorage.pair: There is no companion key/value TDLib type association; data, password, and game_short_name are mutually exclusive variant payload fields.
rejectedStorage.kv: Callback query payloads belong to individual live callback interactions, not to an account-level or global singleton value.

notes: callbackQueryPayloadDataWithPassword.password carries the current user's 2-step verification password; event consumers must not persist or log the payload beyond live request or update handling.

Changes the prior embedded target because updateNewCallbackQuery, updateNewInlineCallbackQuery, and updateNewBusinessCallbackQuery are live update constructors, not durable storage owners under the framework.

reviews.decision: CallDiscardReason is a small union value with no independent key; it is stored only as the discard-reason field on discarded call state and ended-call message content.

indirectTypeUse: MessageContent owner fields including MessageContent.media, MessageReplyTo.content, PollOption.media, PollType.explanation_media, QuickReplyMessage.content, and SponsoredMessage.content can carry messageCall.discard_reason when the nested content variant is messageCall
indirectUpdateUse: message-carrying updates updateNewMessage, updateChatLastMessage, updateChatReplyMarkup, updateMessageSendFailed, updateMessageSendSucceeded, updateActiveLiveLocationMessages, and updateNewGuestQuery can carry Message.content -> messageCall.discard_reason
procedureUse: No function accepts or returns CallDiscardReason directly.
discardCall derives the discarded call outcome from scalar parameters and the resulting reason appears through Call.state.callStateDiscarded.reason and call message content.

Message-returning procedures such as getMessage, getMessages, getMessageLocally, getRepliedMessage, getChatPinnedMessage, getChatMessageByDate, addLocalMessage, sendMessage, and editMessage* can expose Message.content.messageCall.discard_reason through MessageContent, but do not address CallDiscardReason separately.
sendCallRating, sendCallDebugInformation, and sendCallLog use InputCall after discarded-call state flags, not CallDiscardReason as independent stored state.

rejectedStorage.table: CallDiscardReason has no stable id or local key; callDiscardReasonUpgradeToGroupCall.invite_link is payload, not row identity.
rejectedStorage.extend: It is not a one-to-one structural extension of Call, Message, or another owner row; it is a field value under CallState and MessageContent.
rejectedStorage.facet: call_id, chat_id, and message_id identify the owning Call or Message state; there is no separate owner-scoped CallDiscardReason lifecycle.
rejectedStorage.pair: There is no companion key/value shape; the selected constructor and optional invite link form one nested value.
rejectedStorage.kv: The reason belongs to a specific call state or message content payload, not an account-level or global singleton value.
rejectedStorage.event: Discard reasons are part of current call state and durable message content, not live-only signals.

notes: The existing maturity 2 entry's embedded target is supported; this review expands the evidence and keeps prior storage decisions for CallState, MessageContent, Call, and Message as critique input only.

reviews.decision: CallProtocol is a plain protocol capability value with no own identity. Durable storage keeps it only as callStateReady.protocol inside the CallState value embedded in Call.state; acceptCall and createCall use the same shape as request input and do not define separate cached state.

procedureUse: acceptCall(call_id, protocol:callProtocol) accepts local supported protocols for an incoming call; the request input is not stored as CallProtocol state.
createCall(user_id, protocol:callProtocol, is_video) accepts local supported protocols and returns CallId; the stored call state is delivered later through updateCall.
No procedure returns CallProtocol directly or addresses CallProtocol independently. Other call lifecycle procedures identify calls by call_id/InputCall and do not mutate protocol as a separate value.

rejectedStorage.table: CallProtocol has no stable id or local key; layer numbers and library_versions are capability payload, not row identity.
rejectedStorage.extend: It does not structurally extend exactly one owner row; it is one field on the callStateReady variant of CallState.
rejectedStorage.facet: Procedure owner keys such as call_id/user_id belong to acceptCall/createCall request envelopes, while persisted CallProtocol is only the nested CallState.protocol value.
rejectedStorage.pair: There is no companion key/value type; the constructor fields form one embedded value object.
rejectedStorage.kv: The stored value belongs to a specific Call.state snapshot, not an account-level or global singleton key. Procedure inputs do not define a cached local protocol setting.
rejectedStorage.event: CallProtocol represents current call state inside updateCall/Call.state, not a live-only signal whose history can be discarded.

notes: acceptCall/createCall.protocol describes the application's local supported protocols for a request; persist only the protocol received as CallState.protocol from callStateReady.
Agrees with the existing storage entry's embedded CallState.protocol target; maturity 2 evidence adds the distinction between stored call state and procedure-only protocol inputs.

reviews.decision: CallServer is the call relay-server value carried only inside the ready CallState server list. Its server id can identify a selected connection during call teardown, but no update or procedure addresses a CallServer row independently of the owning Call.

procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns CallServer directly.
Call procedures operate by call_id/InputCall and can transition Call.state without addressing CallServer as stored state.
discardCall.connection_id:int64 can report the connection used during the call, but it is scoped by call_id and does not mutate a CallServer row.

rejectedStorage.table: CallServer.id looks row-like, but CallServer appears only as an item in the ready CallState.servers value and has no independent update, fetch, delete, or procedure surface.
rejectedStorage.extend: CallServer is not a one-to-one structural extension of Call or another owner; many server values can appear in one ready call state.
rejectedStorage.facet: The owner key comes from the containing Call/updateCall shape, and the value is an item in a replaced server list rather than one separate owner-scoped aspect record.
rejectedStorage.pair: CallServer is not stored only as an association between a key type and a value type.
rejectedStorage.kv: The value belongs to a specific Call.state payload, not to an account-level or global stable key.
rejectedStorage.event: The server list is current call state delivered through updateCall and needed by call handling, not a live-only signal to emit and discard.

notes: CallServer.id is an id-like nested server identifier, but it is not an independent storage key; keep CallServer embedded under the owning Call.state server list.
CallServer.type can contain WebRTC username/password fields through CallServerType, so avoid duplicating the relay credential payload in any shared server cache.

Keeps the previous embedded decision but changes the target from CallStateReady.servers to CallState.servers so the storage target uses the CallState domain type while still referring to the ready-state servers field. Related accepted targets remain Call as table, CallState embedded at Call.state, and CallServerType embedded at CallServer.type.

reviews.decision: CallServerType is the variant payload stored in CallServer.type. Its constructors describe reflector or WebRTC connection parameters for one CallServer value; it has no independent identity, no owner-scoped key, and no procedure or update addresses it apart from the containing Call state.

procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns CallServerType directly.
createCall and acceptCall can lead to updateCall carrying Call.state -> CallStateReady.servers -> CallServer.type, but they do not address CallServerType separately.
discardCall, sendCallSignalingData, sendCallDebugInformation, sendCallLog, and sendCallRating address Call by call_id, not CallServerType.

rejectedStorage.table: CallServerType has no durable id or stable local key of its own; the fields are parameters of the containing CallServer value.
rejectedStorage.extend: CallServerType does not structurally extend one externally identified owner row; it is a discriminated field value on CallServer.
rejectedStorage.facet: No update or procedure stores or replaces CallServerType as a separate owner-keyed aspect; the update path replaces it only through the containing Call state.
rejectedStorage.pair: CallServerType is not the key or value side of a stored association between two TDLib types.
rejectedStorage.kv: CallServerType is not an account-level or global cached value; each occurrence belongs to a concrete CallServer.type field.
rejectedStorage.event: CallServerType is part of the current Call state carried by updateCall, not a standalone live-only signal.

notes: callServerTypeWebrtc.password and callServerTypeTelegramReflector.peer_tag are embedded call transport credentials; if Call state is persisted, keep them only inside the CallServer.type payload and avoid separate caches or logs.

Confirms the existing maturity 2 embedded decision at CallServer.type. The referenced owner CallServer is also reviewed as embedded at CallStateReady.servers, so the selected target remains inside the server value rather than creating a separate CallServerType record.

reviews.decision: CallState is the variant value stored as Call.state. It has no own identifier, no direct procedure surface, and updates replace it only through updateCall.call on the active Call row keyed by Call.id.

indirectTypeUse: Call is the active call table row keyed by Call.id, and CallState is only its state field.
Nested reviewed targets are CallDiscardReason at CallState.reason, CallProtocol at CallState.protocol, CallServer at CallState.servers, and Error at CallState.error.
procedureUse: No function accepts or returns CallState directly.
createCall(user_id, protocol, is_video) creates an active Call and returns CallId; stored CallState arrives later through updateCall.call.state.
acceptCall(call_id, protocol) mutates the active Call by Call.id and the resulting state is delivered through updateCall.call.state.

discardCall(call_id, is_disconnected, invite_link, duration, is_video, connection_id) ends the active Call by Call.id and can lead to callStateHangingUp or callStateDiscarded in updateCall.call.state.
sendCallSignalingData(call_id, data) addresses the active Call by Call.id; signaling data is not CallState storage.

sendCallRating(call_id:InputCall), sendCallDebugInformation(call_id:InputCall), and sendCallLog(call_id:InputCall) are enabled by callStateDiscarded.need_rating, need_debug_information, and need_log, but they address the call rather than a separate CallState record.

rejectedStorage.table: CallState has no stable id or local key. Call.id identifies the owning active Call row, not a CallState row.
rejectedStorage.extend: CallState is not a one-to-one structural extension of an externally identified owner; it is the discriminated state field inside Call.
rejectedStorage.facet: Although call procedures use call_id, they address the owning Call row. There is only one current Call.state value per Call, and no update or procedure replaces a separate owner-scoped CallState facet.
rejectedStorage.pair: CallState is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape.
rejectedStorage.kv: CallState belongs to a specific active Call row and is not an account-level or global singleton value.
rejectedStorage.event: CallState is current active call state used after update delivery by call lifecycle and reporting procedures, not a live-only signal.

notes: callStateReady contains encryption_key, call config, custom parameters, and server transport details; keep this sensitive live state only inside the active Call.state payload and avoid duplicate caches or logs.

Keeps the existing embedded Call.state decision. Related reviewed targets support the owner shape: Call is a table keyed by id, while CallDiscardReason, CallProtocol, CallServer, CallServerType, and Error are embedded under CallState or its nested fields.

reviews.decision: Store only as an embedded failure/check result value. canPostStory and startLiveStory return fresh result wrappers; updateStoryPostFailed is the durable storage path and attaches the result to the failed Story row.

rejectedStorage.table: No stable identity belongs to CanPostStoryResult; story_count, retry_after, and live-story story_id are payload or references, not row keys.
rejectedStorage.extend: It does not structurally extend Chat or Story; it is a variant value attached to a result or failed story state.
rejectedStorage.facet: The chat_id on canPostStory scopes a fresh check, not a stored Chat-owned aspect; failed posting storage is on the Story row.
rejectedStorage.pair: No companion key/value type forms the persisted record.
rejectedStorage.kv: Not account/global singleton state; values belong to a request result or failed Story state.
rejectedStorage.event: updateStoryPostFailed creates retained failed-story state, so the error type is not purely live-only.

notes: canPostStory(chat_id) is a fresh procedure result and must not create a Chat-scoped cached facet; retained storage comes from updateStoryPostFailed.
updateStoryPostFailed.error_type has no native Story field; storage model adds Story.can_post_story_result on the failed Story row.
canPostStoryResultLiveStoryIsActive.story_id references the active live story and is not a CanPostStoryResult storage key.

fields.name: positions
notes: ChatPosition rows are materialized in telegram_chat_positions.

reviews.decision: Chat is the canonical root chat entity. It has its own durable id, updateNewChat loads a full Chat before a chat identifier is returned, Chat-returning procedures materialize the same row, and chat_id-keyed updates mutate current Chat fields. Store Chat as a table keyed by id; nested values with their own decisions keep their own storage shape instead of being duplicated into the row.

directTypeUse: No other TDLib constructor has a field typed as chat/Chat; Chat is a root entity payload rather than a nested value owned by another type.
directUpdateUse: updateNewChat.chat:chat loads or creates the Chat row before the chat identifier is returned to the application.

chat_id-keyed updates mutate Chat row fields: updateChatAccentColors, updateChatActionBar, updateChatAddedToList, updateChatAvailableReactions, updateChatBackground, updateChatBlockList, updateChatBusinessBotManageBar, updateChatDefaultDisableNotification, updateChatDraftMessage, updateChatEmojiStatus, updateChatHasProtectedContent, updateChatHasScheduledMessages, updateChatIsMarkedAsUnread, updateChatIsTranslatable, updateChatLastMessage, updateChatMessageAutoDeleteTime, updateChatMessageSender, updateChatNotificationSettings, updateChatPendingJoinRequests, updateChatPermissions, updateChatPhoto, updateChatPosition, updateChatReadInbox, updateChatReadOutbox, updateChatRemovedFromList, updateChatReplyMarkup, updateChatTheme, updateChatTitle, updateChatUnreadMentionCount, updateChatUnreadPollVoteCount, updateChatUnreadReactionCount, updateChatVideoChat, updateChatViewAsTopics.
indirectTypeUse: Chat.id is referenced as scalar chat_id by related owner-scoped types such as Message, ChatActiveStories, ChatBoost, ChatRevenueAmount, ChatMember, invite-link, forum-topic, story, and statistics payloads.

Existing related storage decisions keep Chat field payloads in their own shape: Message is a table keyed by chat_id = Chat.id, id; ChatPosition is a facet keyed by chat_id = Chat.id, list_key = ChatList.key; ChatType, ChatPhotoInfo, ChatPermissions, ChatNotificationSettings, ChatAvailableReactions, ChatActionBar, BusinessBotManageBar, VideoChat, DraftMessage, ChatJoinRequestsInfo, ChatBackground, ChatTheme, EmojiStatus, BlockList, MessageSender, and UpgradedGiftColors are embedded values at their Chat fields.
indirectUpdateUse: updateChatLastMessage and updateChatReplyMarkup can carry Message payloads while Message remains the canonical table row keyed by chat_id and id.
updateChatLastMessage, updateChatDraftMessage, and updateChatPosition carry ChatPosition state keyed by chat_id plus ChatList key; order == 0 removes that chat-list position.

chat_id-keyed updates for related state are not Chat row updates: updateChatAction emits ChatAction event state, updateChatOnlineMemberCount carries live opened-chat count, and updateChatActiveStories, updateChatBoost, updateChatMember, updateNewChatJoinRequest, and updateChatRevenueAmount target separate chat-owned records or facets.
procedureUse: Procedures returning Chat: createBasicGroupChat, createNewSecretChat, createNewSupergroupChat, createPrivateChat, createSecretChat, createSupergroupChat, getChat, joinChatByInviteLink, searchChatAffiliateProgram, searchPublicChat, upgradeBasicGroupChatToSupergroupChat.

Procedures that mutate Chat row fields or membership in chat lists by chat_id: addChatToList, deleteChat, deleteChatBackground, deleteChatHistory, deleteChatReplyMarkup, removeChatActionBar, setChatAccentColor, setChatAvailableReactions, setChatBackground, setChatClientData, setChatDraftMessage, setChatEmojiStatus, setChatMessageAutoDeleteTime, setChatMessageSender, setChatNotificationSettings, setChatPermissions, setChatPhoto, setChatProfileAccentColor, setChatTheme, setChatTitle, sendTextMessageDraft, setPinnedChats, toggleChatDefaultDisableNotification, toggleChatHasProtectedContent, toggleChatIsMarkedAsUnread, toggleChatIsPinned, toggleChatIsTranslatable, toggleChatViewAsTopics.

Many other chat_id-keyed procedures use Chat.id as an owner or route for messages, members, stories, topics, invite links, boosts, revenue, statistics, web apps, sponsored messages, and storage cleanup; those do not change Chat table identity.

rejectedStorage.embedded: No durable owner field contains UnconfirmedSession; its only direct use is a top-level account update. Embedding it under Session or Sessions would confuse the fresh active-session list with the maintained first-unconfirmed-session snapshot.
rejectedStorage.extend: UnconfirmedSession is not a structural extension of a single owner row. The update has no external Session owner envelope, and the constructor carries a partial pending-session payload rather than extra fields for an existing Session record.
rejectedStorage.facet: There is no Chat, User, Message, or other domain owner key. The session id is the pending session's action identifier, not an owner key for an owner-scoped aspect.
rejectedStorage.pair: The persistent record is not an association between two TDLib types; the storage key is the domain kv name and the value is the current UnconfirmedSession snapshot.
rejectedStorage.event: updateUnconfirmedSession is not live-only because the current pending session is account state needed after restart for displaying or confirming the session, and null explicitly clears that state.

notes: UnconfirmedSession.id is a real session_id consumed by confirmSession and shares the active Session id namespace, but updateUnconfirmedSession exposes only the first pending session; do not model this update as a multi-row Session or UnconfirmedSession table.

updateUnconfirmedSession.session may be null and the payload contains session/account-state device and location data; clear unconfirmed_session on null and retain only the latest snapshot, not historical values.

reviews.decision: VoiceNote is voice-note media metadata embedded in direct owner payload fields. The constructor carries duration, waveform, mime_type, nullable SpeechRecognitionResult, and a nested File reference, but has no stable VoiceNote id, owner key, or independent lifecycle. Updates and procedures deliver, replace, or mutate it through owner rows or result payloads: MessageContent is replaced by message key, LinkPreviewType is retained through LinkPreview.type, PushMessageContent is retained through NotificationType.content, and speech-recognition procedures address the owning Message rather than a VoiceNote row. Related maturity 2 decisions for File, SpeechRecognitionResult, MessageContent, LinkPreviewType, PushMessageContent, and Audio support keeping VoiceNote embedded while storing canonical nested file state by File.id.

procedureUse: getMessageViewers by chat_id/message_id for voice-note messages
openMessageContent by chat_id/message_id updates voice-note listened state on the owning message content
rateSpeechRecognition by chat_id/message_id rates recognized speech for the owning video-note or voice-note message
recognizeSpeech by chat_id/message_id starts recognition for the owning video-note or voice-note message

rejectedStorage.table: VoiceNote has no own id or stable local key. voice:file points to the canonical File table row, and chat_id/message_id procedures address the owning Message, not a VoiceNote row.
rejectedStorage.extend: VoiceNote is not a one-to-one full-info extension of a single external owner row; it is a media value used by multiple owner payload types.
rejectedStorage.facet: The only external keys connected to voice-note state are owner message keys on updates and procedures. They replace or mutate MessageContent fields and do not define a separate owner-scoped VoiceNote aspect.
rejectedStorage.pair: VoiceNote is not stored only as an association between a key type and a value type.
rejectedStorage.kv: VoiceNote is not an account-level or global singleton value; it belongs to concrete inline-result, link-preview, message, page-block, or push-content payloads.
rejectedStorage.event: VoiceNote is retained as owner payload state whenever the owning result, message, page block, link preview, or notification preview is retained; it is not a live-only signal.

notes: VoiceNote.voice:file is canonical File table state; embedded VoiceNote owners must store a File.id reference and merge through the File table instead of duplicating the nested File payload.

recognizeSpeech and rateSpeechRecognition use chat_id plus message_id; apply resulting state to MessageContent.voice_note.speech_recognition_result when the owner content is a voice note, not to a message-keyed VoiceNote or SpeechRecognitionResult facet.

inputMessageVoiceNote and inputInlineQueryResultVoiceNote are send/input shapes using InputFile or URL fields; they are evidence for procedures only and must not be added as durable VoiceNote storage targets.

Maturity 1 chose the correct embedded target, but it was under-specified: it did not record speech-recognition procedures, updateMessageContentOpened, input-only voice-note shapes, the completed File/SpeechRecognitionResult owner constraints, or the completed MessageContent, LinkPreviewType, and PushMessageContent decisions.

reviews.decision: WebApp is embedded metadata retained only through bot write-access reason payloads and searchWebApp result payloads. The constructor has a short_name local selector but no bot owner id, row id, update, or mutating lifecycle; Web App launch procedures return fresh URLs or WebAppInfo launch state rather than independently stored WebApp rows.

indirectTypeUse: FoundWebApp is returned only by searchWebApp(bot_user_id:int53, web_app_short_name:string) and carries request_write_access and skip_confirmation beside the WebApp payload.
Completed maturity 2 BotWriteAccessAllowReason decision stores BotWriteAccessAllowReason at MessageContent.reason; completed MessageContent decision stores MessageContent as embedded owner content.
Completed maturity 2 Photo and Animation decisions keep WebApp.photo and WebApp.animation as embedded media payloads; nested file identity belongs to File references inside those media payloads.
Completed maturity 2 InternalLinkType and WebAppOpenMode decisions treat internalLinkTypeWebApp.web_app_short_name and Web App open modes as routing/open-parameter payloads, not WebApp storage.
indirectUpdateUse: updateMessageContent.new_content can replace MessageContent.messageBotWriteAccessAllowed.reason -> BotWriteAccessAllowReason.web_app on the owning message.

Message-carrying updates such as updateNewMessage, updateMessageSendSucceeded, updateMessageSendFailed, updateChatLastMessage, updateChatReplyMarkup, updateNewGuestQuery, updateActiveLiveLocationMessages, and updateServiceNotification can carry WebApp through MessageContent.reason.

Business-message, quick-reply, notification, direct-message-topic, saved-message-topic, poll, and file-download updates can inherit the same MessageContent.reason path through their containing message payloads.
updateWebAppMessageSent(web_app_launch_id:int64) is tied to WebAppInfo.launch_id from openWebApp and does not carry or mutate WebApp metadata.
procedureUse: No procedure accepts or returns WebApp directly.

getWebAppLinkUrl(chat_id:int53, bot_user_id:int53, web_app_short_name:string, start_parameter:string, allow_write_access:Bool, parameters:webAppOpenParameters) -> HttpUrl uses the short-name selector to produce a fresh launch URL.
getInternalLink(type:InternalLinkType, is_http:Bool) and getInternalLinkType(link:string) can carry internalLinkTypeWebApp.web_app_short_name as route data; they do not return WebApp metadata.

Message-returning procedures such as getMessage, getMessages, getChatHistory, searchMessages, sendMessage, sendBotStartMessage, forwardMessages, resendMessages, editMessage*, getCallbackQueryMessage, and getMessageLinkInfo can expose WebApp through MessageContent.messageBotWriteAccessAllowed.reason.

Business-message and quick-reply procedures such as sendBusinessMessage, editBusinessMessage*, addQuickReplyShortcutMessage, readdQuickReplyShortcutMessages, and sendQuickReplyShortcutMessages can expose WebApp through nested MessageContent.reason.

openWebApp returns WebAppInfo.launch_id/url, closeWebApp consumes web_app_launch_id, getMainWebApp returns MainWebApp, and getWebAppUrl returns HttpUrl; these launch/open flows do not create, replace, or delete WebApp metadata rows.

answerWebAppQuery, sendWebAppData, sendWebAppCustomRequest, and checkWebAppFileDownload are Web App interaction procedures keyed by query id, bot_user_id, button text, file name, or URL; they do not address WebApp storage.

rejectedStorage.table: WebApp.short_name plus external bot_user_id is used as a lookup selector, but WebApp carries no bot_user_id and TDLib exposes no create, edit, delete, update, or direct get lifecycle for a WebApp row. searchWebApp returns a FoundWebApp result payload, while getWebAppLinkUrl/openWebApp return URL or launch state.
rejectedStorage.extend: WebApp is not a one-to-one structural extension of a Bot/User row; the same shape appears under BotWriteAccessAllowReason.web_app and FoundWebApp.web_app.
rejectedStorage.facet: There is no separate bot_user_id-keyed WebApp aspect with its own update shape. bot_user_id scopes lookup and launch procedures, while stored occurrences are ordinary embedded payload fields.
rejectedStorage.pair: WebApp is not stored only as an association between a key shape and a value shape; the short-name selector is scalar route input, not a paired TDLib key type.
rejectedStorage.kv: WebApp is not account-level singleton or global catalog state keyed by a stable domain name; retained values belong to concrete reason/result owner payloads.
rejectedStorage.event: WebApp metadata can be retained with message content or a FoundWebApp result payload, so it is not only a live interaction signal.

notes: WebApp.short_name is used with external bot_user_id by searchWebApp and getWebAppLinkUrl, which makes it look like an owner-scoped table key; under the reviewed schema those calls return fresh lookup or launch data and do not establish durable WebApp rows.

Maturity 1 chose the correct embedded target but was too thin: it did not critique the bot_user_id + short_name table-candidate path, distinguish searchWebApp from launch/open flows, record updateWebAppMessageSent as WebAppInfo launch state rather than WebApp metadata, or tie WebApp.photo/WebApp.animation to the completed Photo and Animation decisions.

reviews.decision: WebAppOpenMode is a fieldless enum-like selector with no identifier, owner key, or row lifecycle. The retained storage path is the mode field on InternalLinkType web-app routing variants when an InternalLinkType is stored inside its accepted embedded owners. MainWebApp.mode and WebAppOpenParameters.mode are direct open-call result/input payloads and do not add durable storage targets.

indirectUpdateUse: message and reply-markup updates can carry Message.reply_markup -> InlineKeyboardButtonType.target_chat -> TargetChat.link -> InternalLinkType.mode: updateActiveLiveLocationMessages, updateActiveNotifications, updateBusinessMessageEdited, updateChatLastMessage, updateChatReplyMarkup, updateDirectMessagesChatTopic, updateFileAddedToDownloads, updateMessageEdited, updateMessageSendFailed, updateMessageSendSucceeded, updateNewBusinessCallbackQuery, updateNewBusinessMessage, updateNewChat, updateNewGuestQuery, updateNewMessage, updateNotification, updateNotificationGroup, updateQuickReplyShortcut, updateQuickReplyShortcutMessages, updateSavedMessagesTopic

getInternalLinkType(link:string) returns InternalLinkType values that can include InternalLinkType.mode as routing payloads
getMainWebApp(chat_id:int53, bot_user_id:int53, start_parameter:string, parameters:webAppOpenParameters) -> MainWebApp returns MainWebApp.mode as a fresh open result
getWebAppLinkUrl, getWebAppUrl, and openWebApp accept WebAppOpenParameters.mode as open-call input
getUserFullInfo, getPremiumFeatures, getPremiumState, and getWebPageInstantView can return owner payloads that contain InternalLinkType.mode

send/edit message, answer inline/web-app, quick-reply, and message lookup procedures can carry InternalLinkType.mode through ReplyMarkup -> TargetChat.link paths; schema scan found 97 procedure paths to WebAppOpenMode

rejectedStorage.table: WebAppOpenMode constructors have no id, local key, or mutable row lifecycle; the mode value is only a fieldless selector inside owner payloads.
rejectedStorage.extend: WebAppOpenMode does not structurally extend one owner row; the same enum value is reused in internal-link routing payloads and open-call input/result payloads.
rejectedStorage.facet: No update or procedure addresses a separate owner-scoped WebAppOpenMode aspect. Procedure owner keys such as chat_id and bot_user_id scope web-app opening calls, not stored mode records.
rejectedStorage.pair: There is no companion key/value type whose association defines WebAppOpenMode storage.
rejectedStorage.kv: The mode is not an account-level singleton or catalog keyed by a stable domain name; it belongs to specific routing or open-call payloads.
rejectedStorage.event: When retained, the mode is part of an embedded InternalLinkType payload rather than a live-only signal; open-call input/result occurrences are fresh procedure payloads, not events.

notes: MainWebApp.mode and WebAppOpenParameters.mode are intentionally omitted from the storage target because they are fresh getMainWebApp output and web-app open input; do not create a persisted current web-app mode or account kv from those procedure payloads.

Maturity 2 keeps the maturity 1 embedded kind but narrows the target from InternalLinkType.mode, MainWebApp.mode, WebAppOpenParameters.mode to InternalLinkType.mode. The maturity 1 review treated fresh open-call result/input payloads as storage targets; this review keeps them as procedure evidence only. Related completed maturity 2 decisions inspected: InternalLinkType is embedded at its accepted owner fields, TargetChat is embedded at InlineKeyboardButtonType.target_chat and InternalLinkType.target_chat, BotInfo is embedded at UserFullInfo.bot_info, and WebApp is embedded only under BotWriteAccessAllowReason.web_app and FoundWebApp.web_app.
